articles.title: How the 30-day savings rule can help you stop impulse spending and save more money
articles.summary: The 30-day savings rule is a simple strategy that helps you avoid overspending and get closer to reaching your savings goals. Here's how it works.
articles.body:

If you struggle with impulsive spending, there's a strategy that may help. It's called the 30-day savings rule — a budgeting strategy designed to curb impulse spending and help you save more money. Here's how it works.

The 30-day savings rule is a simple strategy to cut down on overspending. It works like this: When you're tempted to make an impulse purchase, you commit to waiting 30 days before going through with it.

Of course, at the end of those 30 days, you may decide that you do, in fact, want to make the purchase. The 30-day rule isn't necessarily going to stop you from spending money completely. But it will force you to slow down, be more mindful about your purchases, and prevent you from buying items that you don't really need or want.

Extra time can give you the perspective you need to determine whether or not your purchase is necessary. It can also give you a chance to comparison shop, dig for coupons, or wait for the item to go on sale.

Pros and cons of the 30-day savings rule

Overall, you'll probably find that the 30-day savings rule has a positive impact on your finances. However, there are some drawbacks to consider, too.

Reduces impulse spending: Waiting 30 days gives you time to consider whether you truly need or want something rather than making an emotional or spontaneous purchase.

Helps you save money: By avoiding unnecessary purchases, you can free up money to put toward your emergency fund, retirement savings, debt repayment, or other financial goals.

Prevents buyer's remorse: Giving yourself time to think before making a purchase can reduce the likelihood of regretting it later.

Easy to implement: Unlike some budgeting strategies, the 30-day rule doesn't require complicated calculations, special apps, or tracking every dollar you spend.

Helps identify spending patterns: Keeping a list of purchases you're considering can reveal which types of products or experiences tend to trigger impulse spending.

Not always practical for certain purchases: Waiting 30 days isn't realistic when you need to replace a broken appliance, purchase necessary clothing, or cover another urgent expense.

You could miss out on legitimate savings: Delaying a purchase could mean missing a limited-time sale or promotional offer. But remember that a special deal only saves you money if you were already planning to buy the item in the first place.

Doesn't guarantee you'll save money: Simply postponing purchases won't necessarily improve your finances if you eventually buy everything on your list. To maximize your savings, consider transferring the money you would have spent on unwanted purchases into a savings account.

Can feel overly restrictive: Waiting an entire month for every discretionary purchase may feel frustrating, especially if you have enough room in your budget to comfortably afford smaller purchases.

How much money can the 30-day savings rule save you?

Sure, a last-minute pack of gum at the register may not put a dent in your budget. But impulsive spending can add up, especially if you're not taking the time to think through more expensive purchases.

According to research by Capital One Shopping , the average consumer spends $254 per month on impulse buys, for an annual total of $3,045. That's money that could be put toward paying off debt, building an emergency fund, or even funding a vacation.

For example, say you take that $254 and deposit it into a high-yield savings account each month instead of spending it. If your account earns 4% APY, you'd make an extra $57 in interest over the course of the year. Plus, you'd end up with more than $3,000 set aside as a safety net, which can go a long way toward improving your financial well-being .

Of course, your personal spending habits will dictate how much you can save by implementing this rule. But even small changes can have a positive impact on your finances.

How to implement the 30-day savings rule

Let's say you're shopping, and an item catches your eye that wasn't actually on your shopping list — or even on your radar until this very moment. Before you commit to the purchase, open up your phone and make a note of the item, along with where it can be purchased, the price information, and any relevant links (if it's online).

Then leave the item and plan to revisit that note in 30 days. In the meantime, ask yourself a few key questions:

How would this purchase impact my budget and savings goals?

First, it's important to consider whether you can truly afford the purchase. You should have enough disposable income to cover the cost without impacting your short-term budget or long-term goals.

Can I get this item for a lower price somewhere else?

Comparison shopping is a great way to save, but it isn't possible when you make a purchase impulsively. By adopting the 30-day rule, you give yourself enough time to browse online and hit a few different stores to see if the item you want is available for a lower price somewhere else.

Are there any upcoming sales or discounts?

Do some research to see if the particular store you're shopping with has an upcoming sale or if there's a coupon available that can help you save.

Maybe there's a similar or off-brand version that doesn't cost as much. It can be easy to get swayed by high-end labels sometimes, but there are often generic alternatives to most items that cost a fraction of the price for the same end result.

How many hours would I have to work to pay for this item?

Thinking about purchases in terms of your time can help put things into perspective. For example, if something costs $100 and you have the money to pay for it, you may not think twice. But what if, instead, you thought about pricing in terms of how long you would need to work to earn that money? Say you earn $15 per hour — six hours of work to pay for an impulse buy may not seem worth it after all.

When faced with the opportunity to buy something that catches your eye, it can be hard to say no — especially if you have the money in your bank account to cover the splurge.

However, giving yourself time and space from an unplanned purchase might actually help you decide if you need it or if it was just a momentary lapse in judgment. Depending on the price tag, taking this pause can save you from derailing your budget.

articles.title: Here's what Nvidia's stock struggles could mean for 401(k) accounts
articles.summary: Nvidia's share value initially fell nearly 10% over the past two days.
articles.body:
Shares of Nvidia are down about 8% in value this week since the computer chip giant said over the weekend it opened an investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang amid allegations of a Chinese intelligence-gathering effort targeting him.

The selloff incurred losses not only for direct Nvidia shareholders, but also for many everyday people's 401(k) accounts, analysts told ABC News. Those accounts often hold index funds, which track stock indexes like the Nasdaq 100 and the S&P 500.

Such indexes, in turn, are often weighted toward major companies like Nvidia, the second-largest corporation in the world as measured by market capitalization, following Apple.

Analysts who spoke to ABC News acknowledged short-term losses suffered by many 401(k) portfolios as a result of the stock slide, but the experts differed about the extent to which those losses should concern account holders.

Some analysts emphasized the relatively large share taken up by Nvidia in index funds and the risk the allegations about Huang pose for the company. Others stressed the durability of the stock market over time and the capacity for a diversified portfolio to absorb losses by a single company, even one the size of Nvidia.

"Nvidia does make up a big chunk of some important indexes," Reena Aggarwal, professor of finance and director of the Georgetown Psaros Center for Financial Markets and Policy, told ABC News. "Obviously, that company is extremely important, but I would think long term and not about day-to-day market fluctuations."

The Nvidia board initiated an "independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," the company said in a statement Sunday.

The investigation will be overseen by a "committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel," Nvidia added.

Huang "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the Nvidia statement noted.

The Republican chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Rep. Brian Mast, told ABC News on Tuesday that he's prepared to subpoena Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he did not respond by Wednesday to a request from several House Republicans for a closed-door briefing on Huang's reported relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

Shares of Nvidia dropped nearly 10% in value combined over two days at the outset of this week, following the company's announcement on Sunday of a probe into Huang's alleged actions. In early trading on Wednesday, Nvidia rose 2.5%, recovering a portion of the losses.

articles.title: World oil market is returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover, IEA says
articles.summary: LONDON, Nov 13 - The world oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, the International Energy Agency said on Friday, as Middle...
articles.body:
LONDON, Nov 13 - The world oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, the International Energy Agency said on Friday, as Middle East exports recover ‌faster than global oil demand despite continued attacks on shipping.

The agency also gave more details of remaining volumes to ‌come from a record release of oil from its members' emergency reserves pledged in March, saying 71 million barrels would be made available by the ​end of February including 15 million barrels of diesel to ease market tightness.

Oil supply will average 105 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, the Paris-based agency, which advises industrialised countries, said in a monthly report, 1.7 million bpd higher than forecast demand. The IEA had previously forecast a fourth-quarter supply deficit.

"The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing ‌demand for the first time since the ⁠outbreak of the war in Iran," the agency said in the report.

Oil prices reversed earlier gains after the IEA report was released at 0900 GMT. Brent crude was last down 0.1% at $95.71 a ⁠barrel.

The report follows signs that Gulf oil producers are recovering exports disrupted since the start of the war in late February by using workarounds such as so-called dark crossings through the Strait of Hormuz, where tankers switch off tracking signals to evade attack.

The OPEC+ ​group, which ​includes the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies such ​as Russia, pumped 41.23 million bpd of crude ‌in October, OPEC said on Wednesday, up about 2.04 million bpd from September and 97% of the pre-war February volume.

Other analysts have also forecast a return to excess supply, despite the lack of a resolution to the Iran war and continuing tanker attacks in the Gulf. JPMorgan last week forecast a global surplus of 1.4 million bpd in October.

High oil prices have also curbed demand this year, helping tip the balance into a surplus. World oil demand is ‌forecast to fall by 2.7 million bpd in 2026 to 102.3 million bpd before rebounding ​by 2 million bpd in 2027, the IEA said, little changed from ​its previous forecasts.

As well as rising output from OPEC+, ​the IEA flagged supply rising from outside the group.

Production from the United States, Canada, Brazil, Argentina and Guyana ‌will rise by 1.6 million bpd this year, ​the IEA said. In 2027, global ​supply is projected to rise by 6.6 million bpd to 108.1 million bpd, led by a further recovery in Gulf output.

articles.title: Trump bought Nvidia shares, then cleared path for chip sales to China: Report
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump bought millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares before taking decisions that eased restrictions on the chipmaker's exports to
articles.body: US President Donald Trump bought millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares before taking decisions that eased restrictions on the chipmaker's exports to China, an analysis of his financial disclosures has found.According to an analysis by anti-corruption group DeKleptocracy, Trump's disclosures show he purchased between $1 million and $5 million worth of Nvidia stock in the days before his administration scrapped a Biden-era export rule in May 2025.The rule, known as the diffusion rule, was intended to restrict exports of advanced US-made artificial intelligence (AI) chips to China over concerns that Beijing could use the technology to develop superior AI capabilities. Its removal opened the way for Nvidia to expand sales in a market that accounted for about a quarter of its revenue between 2010 and 2022.Nvidia shares rose in value after Trump announced the reversal. His disclosures also showed purchases of shares in other technology companies, including Apple, Meta and Microsoft.The president's Nvidia investments continued as his administration moved to ease restrictions further. In December 2025, Trump announced that Nvidia would be allowed to sell its H200 chips to China. The US commerce department approved the move in January 2026.The decision drew criticism over the potential implications for US national security. Experts said the H200 chips were among Nvidia's most advanced products and were six times more powerful than the chips available in China at the time, the Guardian reported.The council on foreign relations warned that their sale could “supercharge” China's future AI factories and strengthen the US's rival.Trump's financial disclosures indicate that he made at least three Nvidia stock purchases in the days after announcing the H200 decision. Each transaction was valued between $250,001 and $500,000. He appears to have made dozens of Nvidia-related stock transactions since taking office, with some ranking among his largest purchases.The stock purchases have come amid separate scrutiny of Nvidia's links to an alleged Chinese intelligence operation. Reports have alleged that Alice Huang, described as a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang, and that her company, Megaspeed, obtained billions of dollars' worth of the chipmaker's products.Trump was briefed twice by US intelligence officials on their assessment that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset, but did not act on it, according to The Guardian.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Virginia couple walks away from 2.7% mortgage on $595K house after Ramit Sethi maps out a $6.2M alternative
articles.summary: A Virginia couple is walking away from their low 2.7% mortgage on a $595K house after speaking with finance author Ramit Sethi.
articles.body:
Yard work takes up about eight hours of Chloe and Jake's time on a typical weekend. Their four-bedroom Virginia house comes with an office and a pool and sits on 1.5 acres. Around the 1990s, Chloe told Ramit Sethi of " I Will Teach You to Be Rich ," it belonged to one of Jake's uncles — a multimillionaire whose grounds had two koi ponds and a staff of gardeners.

When Jake's parents sold them the house in late 2020, much of that landscaping had gone untended. They skipped the inspection and took the place as is. Chloe is now a busy 32-year-old software engineer, and Jake, 30, is a senior manager in an engineering department. They both want out.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 5 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

"Everybody that we talk to is like, you know, homeownership is the dream," Chloe told personal finance author Sethi on the Nov. 3 episode of his podcast. "And I'm like, are we just dumb?"

They locked in 2.7% when the average 30-year fixed rate tracked by Freddie Mac, the Virginia-based mortgage buyer, was near its record low of 2.65% in January 2021. Freddie Mac's Nov. 12 survey put that average at 7.11% . For the second quarter of 2026, data from the Federal Housing Finance Agency, which regulates Freddie Mac, shows just 19.2% of outstanding U.S. mortgages under 3% . Chloe had gone back and forth for about eight months because she didn't want to add selling to the list of money mistakes they'd already made.

How they ended up in a house appraised at $595K with no inspection

Back then, they were paying $2,400 a month in rent. Jake figured rates that low would never return and saw rent as wasted money. The house appraised at $595K, above the $500K they'd budgeted.

The mortgage went in Jake's name alone. By his account, averaging their two credit scores would have put them under a 760 cutoff, so Chloe was left off the loan.

"Honestly, signing that though, like I wanted to throw up," he said of the roughly half-million-dollar loan.

Their monthly payment with escrow has gone from $2,990 to $3,072. Once maintenance and other costs are added, the couple estimated they spend closer to $4,500.

Then came what Chloe calls their "schemes." Two years ago, an $80K home equity loan paid for renovations meant to turn the house into an Airbnb rental, though Chloe admitted they barely looked at the area's rental demand, which she said is soft. They also bought a 44-foot, eight-year-old RV for $50K and a new truck to tow it.

articles.title: Anthropic IPO to test Wall Street's faith in AI as skepticism mounts
articles.summary: Anthropic seeks a valuation of approximately $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion.
articles.body:
There were no rockets decking Wall Street bank lobbies this past week, unlike the spectacle surrounding SpaceX's blockbuster June listing.

Instead, bankers marketing Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) potentially record-breaking initial public offering this week faced an unusually turbulent backdrop as Treasury yields surged and a widespread Microsoft Outlook outage hampered communications, all during — the biggest disruption of all — the sudden ousting of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is among Anthropic's biggest investors and chip suppliers.

At a JPMorgan Chase investor event Friday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei outlined a future in which AI could help make diseases such as cancer and Alzheimer's relics of the past, while devising entirely new markets in scientific research, robotics, and cybersecurity.

"We can have a much more beautiful world ... It sounds starry-eyed. It sounds crazy. I really do believe it," Amodei told JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon.

Yet Amodei struck a more restrained tone about the company's move to go public, saying he hopes the company will "underpromise and overdeliver."

"We're not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day or what market conditions we go public into," he added.

The comments come as Anthropic seeks a valuation of approximately $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion, below the $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion figures investors had contemplated just weeks earlier.

The offering, expected to begin trading on Thursday, Nov. 19, could provide one of the clearest tests yet of investors' appetite for AI at a moment when enthusiasm for the broader trade is showing signs of cracks.

The contrast between Anthropic's lofty ambitions and Amodei's measured approach to the IPO has also been apparent in Wall Street's marketing campaign.

The lobbies of JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, and Goldman Sachs have been decorated to welcome the startup, according to people familiar with the arrangements. But the displays are more subdued than the digital displays and skyscraper illuminations of rocket ships Wall Street bank visitors witnessed during SpaceX's June IPO, or the meteorite exhibit at JPMorgan's Manhattan headquarters.

Banks are nevertheless mounting a substantial effort to attract investors.

At Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the two banks leading the offering, Anthropic executives met with institutional investors earlier this week. Goldman is also planning an event next week for wealth management clients, where the bank's president, John Waldron, is expected to interview Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and CFO Krishna Rao, according to a people familiar with the plans.

articles.title: AMD Just Had Its Biggest Run Against Nvidia Since 1999. Can It Survive Earnings?
articles.summary: AMD stock beat Nvidia by a record margin over 5 days, then fell 8.75% with Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings due November 17.
articles.body:
AMD outperformed Nvidia by 53.2 percentage points over five trading days, according to The Kobeissi Letter. That is the widest gap between the two chipmakers since Nvidia went public in January 1999.

That lead met its first test on Friday, when AMD stock fell 8.75%. Nvidia's November 17 earnings report now sets up the next one.

How Nvidia's Leadership Crisis Fed the AMD Rally

AMD rallied 44.7% over the 5-day stretch while Nvidia dropped 8.5%, according to The Kobeissi Letter. The previous record gap, set in April 2016, stood at 49.9 percentage points.

So far this year, the AMD vs Nvidia gap is even wider. AMD stock has gained 149.4% since January 1, while Nvidia is down 12.7%, as of Friday's close. That puts the year-to-date gap at about 162 percentage points.

The run overlapped with growing scrutiny of Jensen Huang, who quit Nvidia as CEO on November 12. The company named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent replacement.

AMD also gave buyers its own numbers to work with. Its third-quarter revenue rose 45% from a year earlier to a record $13.4 billion. Data center sales nearly doubled to $8.5 billion.

"AMD has been a major beneficiary of Nvidia's historic volatility," The Kobeissi Letter posted on X.

Friday's Sell-Off Hands the Next Move to Nvidia

The record run lost some ground in Friday's session. AMD closed at $534.06, down from $585.30, and slipped another 2.41% to $521.20 after hours.

Chip stocks sold off as a group. The 10-year Treasury yield remained above 5% after October's producer price index. Rising yields tend to hit growth stocks hardest, since their value rests on profits expected years ahead.

Trading volume reached 48.6 million shares, nearly double the 3-month average. Analysts at The Motley Fool linked part of the drop to profit-taking after the surge.

The after-hours price now sits just above $514. BeInCrypto's AMD stock price analysis marked that level as the line that would break the bullish setup.

Nvidia earnings land on Tuesday after the US market closes. The company guided for $108 billion in third-quarter revenue, plus or minus 2%. Analysts polled by LSEG expect about $109.2 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.48 per share.

The quarter closed on October 25, before Huang resigned, so the results will reflect his tenure. The guidance for the next quarter will be the first issued with Kress as interim CEO.

Solid results and guidance could draw investors back to Nvidia. A weak one could drag the whole chip group lower, AMD included, because Friday showed both stocks still trade together.

articles.title: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has over 100,000 signatures, including some big names
articles.summary: Organizers of the petition say some 50,000 shareholders and 5,000 current Nvidia employees, have signed their petition to bring back Jensen Huang.
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting to an affair.

Nvidia is investigating whether the affair was a "foreign intelligence effort."

Over 100,000 people have now signed a petition to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and others.

Some people aren't ready to let former CEO Jensen Huang go.

A petition to reinstate Huang as Nvidia's CEO has over 108,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon, including prominent tech leaders such as billionaire Elon Musk and Replit CEO Amjad Masad. Both executives promoted the petition on X.

A website for the campaign, dubbed "Stand with Jensen," said the list includes more than 58,000 shareholders, more than 5,600 current Nvidia employees, and over 1,000 former employees.

It also, to be fair, included "Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor" and "Xi Jingping," a possibly misspelled reference to the Chinese leader. In an X post on Saturday, the organizers said they were "actively working" to remove fake signatures.

One Nvidia employee who signed the letter told Business Insider that similar efforts are happening inside the company. A post with similar sentiments appeared on an internal portal where employees can submit questions and suggestions, they said.

Wired reported that the post had garnered 1,600 comments as of Thursday — a figure that has now more than doubled, the employee said.

Earlier this week, Nvidia's board of directors said it opened an investigation into whether Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort" after he admitted to having an affair in a letter to staffers. Days later, Huang resigned after reports he had another affair with an Nvidia executive, and the board appointed Colette Kress , executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO until they find a permanent successor.

An October report by The New York Times said Huang had developed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang , a tech executive at Megaspeed in Singapore. The Times reported that US intelligence officials said she may be a spy for the Chinese government. China has since denied that claim. On Thursday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Department of Justice had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a spy.

The "Stand with Jensen" organizers said in an open letter to Nvidia's board posted to its website that they believe the board removed Huang without an investigation and "meaningful due process."

"We have not been shown evidence substantiating the espionage allegation. After thirty-three years pouring his heart and soul into NVIDIA, Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice," they said.

articles.title: Why Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has 22 meetings a day — and what you can learn from it
articles.summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan is a tech warrior. Learn from him.
articles.body:
If you want to get ahead in business, sometimes you have to set aside the concept of having an amazing work-life balance.

Leaders at the highest levels of corporate America have told me repeatedly that work-life balance is great in theory, but it doesn't exist if you want to get big things done. They say you have to win every second, every minute, every hour, and every day to get ahead.

Take Intel ( INTC ) CEO Lip-Bu Tan as an example. More than a year into the top job at Intel, the tech veteran and former basketball player is having grueling days at 66 that most 21-year-olds couldn't keep up with. For Tan, maximizing time is of the essence in trying to turn around the iconic Intel.

"I broke my own record. I had 22 meetings a day for the first few months [on the job], and because time is not on my side," Tan said at Yahoo Finance Invest this week.

Under Tan's leadership, Intel has won deserved praise on Wall Street. The company's execution and competitiveness in its core client and data center compute markets have improved. Next-generation manufacturing execution has steadied, notably yields, manufacturability, foundry process, and advanced packaging.

These are all metrics foundational to the Intel comeback story, and the Street tracks them like a hawk.

The company did have a stumble recently, however, with its third quarter earnings report.

The stock collapsed after Intel's forecast for fourth quarter sales fell well shy of expectations due to a worse-than-expected decline in PC sales. At the center of the PC weakness is a shortage of memory chips, which are being snapped up by AI hyperscalers, pushing prices up and causing consumers to delay purchases.

At the same time, an explosion at Intel's Kiryat Gat chip fabrication facility in Israel in early October will cost the company about $600 million in lost sales across two quarters, the company said. The lost sales include 10-nanometer server shipments.

Why the biggest risk for investors in 2027 isn't Nvidia — it's inflation

From SpaceX's IPO to orbital data centers, execs say industry's future still in 'earliest innings'

Bill Ackman says Microsoft's position is 'really, really strong' as Anthropic pushes into enterprise software

Intel stock is down 42% over the past month.

Tan said he is having fewer meetings each day, but still has the engineering team report directly to him. His daily schedule is a masterclass in scheduling, interspersed with strategic moments to reset and recover.

"My routine is very simple, and it depends on what day and what time the first meeting is," Tan said. "I usually have swimming and the gym. I usually take about one hour, and so if the meeting starts at seven, then I wake up at 5:30 a.m., and then I go to swim and the gym, and that's also my time of meditation. Then I start my days either with a conference call or physical meeting. My day usually is long until almost 1 o'clock in the morning, … so that is kind of a lot of meetings, a lot of phone calls, and a lot of get-togethers. Then the weekend usually is my more effective time, so that's where I deep dive with my team, deep dive with some of the areas I want to focus, and then so Saturday and Sunday usually I am kind of tied up."

articles.title: Strong economy drives NH toll to record 6,640cr in Oct
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Toll collection on national highways and expressways touched an all-time high of around Rs 6,640 crore in Oct, indicating stronger economic
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Toll collection on national highways and expressways touched an all-time high of around Rs 6,640 crore in Oct, indicating stronger economic activity and increased movement of vehicles across the country's highway network.The collection of user fee was around 16% higher than the Rs 5,715 crore recorded in Oct 2025. The previous highest monthly toll revenue was Rs 6,185 crore, collected in May this year. Going by the trend, the total toll collection is projected to be around Rs 74,000 crore, officials said.A significant change was also visible in the mode of payment, with cash collections dropping sharply to barely Rs 4 crore last month from Rs 84 crore in the corresponding month last year. At the same time, payments through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) rose to around Rs 100 crore in Oct, against no such collection a year ago.The sharp decline in cash transactions follows govt directions to move away from cash payments for highway user fees and use FASTag or UPI as the default modes for paying the user charge. Officials said stricter monitoring was being carried out to ensure that cash is completely phased out as a mode of toll payment. "End of cash transaction will eliminate any scope of malpractices. More people are also opting for FASTag Annual Passes, which is a good sign," said another official. Growing adoption of electronic toll collection has reduced dependence on cash at toll plazas. articles.title: US trade deal talks near finishing line: EAM
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar Saturday said many of the pending issues in the trade deal with the US were \"not so much at our end\" and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar Saturday said many of the pending issues in the trade deal with the US were "not so much at our end" and that negotiations are near the "finishing line"."Well, it's certainly our hope, and in many ways anticipation that we are at the last stretch," he said.The comments come a week after a team of US officials came to India to discuss the customs and trade facilitation chapter with India, which is waiting for clarity on what the new tariff framework will be after the US Supreme Court ruled that US President Donald Trump's "reciprocal tariffs" were illegal. His comments may be an indication that govt is awaiting the next step from the Trump administration - which is conducting a second Section 301 probe against over a dozen countries for structural overcapacity.For several weeks now, officials from both sides have been stating that talks are in the final lap, with Trump also saying the deal with India may be different from other deals. "For us, the key is that we want a trade deal which is beneficial, is balanced and which would give us a comparative advantage over groups of comparable economies," Jaishankar said at the HT Leadership Summit.The repeated comments have raised hopes of the first tranche of the deal being announced soon, although things can move only after the US Trade Representative completes the second probe. PM Modi and Trump are due to meet in the US next month.Jaishankar said the US is India's biggest market and having the trade deal with it would benefit the country. "For the US, Trump is obviously looking to do a whole set of bilateral deals to improve markets for himself. Now, the challenge is to find a landing point.""I think this is not something which could have been done quickly, because these are serious issues; people's jobs and people's lives are at stake."Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Online platforms liable for banned listings: Panel
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An online platform cannot hide behind its intermediary status to evade responsibility under consumer protection law and must exercise due
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An online platform cannot hide behind its intermediary status to evade responsibility under consumer protection law and must exercise due diligence before allowing listings of prohibited, hazardous and regulated products, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has ruled.The order will have wider implications and act as a deterrent to the sale of hazardous items such as explosives, acids and jammers that pose a danger, as well as other regulated products. Online platforms and e-commerce companies often cite their intermediary status to escape responsibility and action in such cases.The NCDRC passed the order while hearing appeals filed by Weblink.in against two orders of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) concerning the online listing of ammonium nitrate, picric acid and pentaerythritol tetranitrate. The authority had imposed a penalty of Rs 20 lakh on the platform in the two cases.The commission upheld the penalty imposed by the authority. In its order passed earlier this week, the commission said the platform could not claim immunity under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act on the ground that it had no “actual knowledge” of the listings. It also said the company could not plead “selective diligence”.In one of the orders, the commission said, “The platform has its own list of do’s and don’ts, and it is evident they are not unaware of the precautions while facilitating transactions through their platforms in respect of hazardous substances or such prohibited items detrimental to the life of consumers. The argument that they are not obliged to verify licences as there is no such statutory obligation deserves rejection as the platform has the obligation to take reasonable care and exercise due diligence while allowing its platform to be utilised for such advertisement...”Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: 'Cashback' da reforma tributária: cerca de 70 milhões de pessoas começam a receber o benefício em janeiro; veja o que é preciso fazer | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Cashback' tem por objetivo reduzir desigualdades de renda no país. Projeções apontam que cerca de uma em cada três pessoas no Brasil têm direito ao benefício.
articles.summary: 'Cashback' tem por objetivo reduzir desigualdades de renda no país. Projeções apontam que cerca de uma em cada três pessoas no Brasil têm direito ao benefício.
articles.body:
O governo federal começa a operacionalizar em janeiro o chamado "cashback" da reforma tributária, mecanismo que prevê a devolução ou abatimento de parte do novo imposto federal sobre o consumo para famílias de baixa renda.

Segundo a Receita Federal, as contas de energia elétrica, água, gás canalizado, esgoto e telefone já virão no primeiro mês de 2027 com dedução de 100% da Contribuição Sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS) do governo federal — que até o momento tem a alíquota estimada de 11,3%.

Exemplo de fatura de energia elétrica — Foto: Receita Federal

O mecanismo do "cashback" também prevê a devolução de 20% do imposto pago no restante dos produtos pela população carente, menos aqueles sobre os quais incide o imposto seletivo, conhecido como "imposto do pecado" (cigarros, bebidas alcoólicas e açucaradas, entre outros).

Ainda de acordo com a Receita Federal, essa devolução será feita, inicialmente, de forma trimestral. A primeira parcela deverá ser paga até 25 de abril, abrangendo os valores acumulados nos meses de janeiro, fevereiro e março. Em um segundo momento, sem data definida, os repasses passarão a ser mensais.

Aprovado na reforma tributária, o mecanismo tem por objetivo reduzir as desigualdades de renda no país diante da manutenção de uma elevada carga tributária sobre o consumo - algo que penaliza principalmente a população mais pobre. A estimativa é que sejam pagos R$ 10 bilhões em 2027.

Dados oficiais de junho deste ano indicam que há 27,7 milhões de famílias beneficiárias do "cashback", englobando um total de cerca de 70 milhões de pessoas . Projeções apontam, portanto, que cerca de uma em cada três pessoas no Brasil têm direito ao "cashback" da reforma tributária.

"Ninguém precisa correr até uma unidade da Receita Federal, qualquer instituição bancária, qualquer portal para pedir, para se inscrever no 'cashback'. A inclusão no 'cashback' é automática", disse José Carlos de Araújo, gerente-substituto do projeto "cashback" da Receita Federal ao g1.

Cerca de 70 milhões de pessoas começam a receber 'cashback' de tributos em janeiro — Foto: Arte/g1

Pelas regras da reforma tributária, o abatimento e a devolução do imposto serão direcionados à população de baixa renda inscrita no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico) com renda renda per capita (por pessoa) inferior a meio salário-mínimo, R$ 820,5 atualmente. Esse limite será reajustado em janeiro.

De acordo com as informações da Receita Federal, beneficiários do "cashback" da reforma tributária devem tomar cuidado com os seguintes pontos para obter o benefício:

Possuir inscrição em situação regular no Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas (CPF), da Receita Federal.

Manter seus dados atualizados no CadÚnico, inclusive o endereço correto para ter direito ao abatimento nas contas de água, luz e gás encanado, por exemplo.

Pedir a nota fiscal e colocar seu CPF na nota para todas as compras a partir de 1º de janeiro para conseguir a devolução do imposto cobrado.

A Receita Federal lembra que o benefício é concedido para os "responsáveis pela unidade familiar" inscritos no CadÚnico, que receberá a devolução de parte do imposto pago nas compras feitas por todas as pessoas do mesmo domicílio.

O órgão informou, ainda, os beneficiários também vão poder acompanhar o uso do "cashback", quer seja de abatimento ou devolução, por meio do aplicativo da Receita Federal disponível nos sistemas IOS ou Android.

Aplicativo da Receita Federal disponibilizará acompanhamento do 'cashback' — Foto: Receita Federal

De acordo com a Receita Federal, a forma como será feita a devolução de parte do imposto do governo federal sobre o consumo nas compras da população de baixa renda ainda está em discussão. A definição acontecerá até abril do próximo ano, quando se iniciam os pagamentos.

Via Poupança Social na Caixa Econômica Federal , método mais comum de recebimento de benefícios do governo atualmente;

Caso o beneficiário não tenha poupança social, o depósito deverá ser feito via PIX em qualquer instituição financeira.

"Esse cidadão aqui, ele não tem Poupança Social na Caixa. Então, vai pagar por PIX. Então, a pessoa tem que ir no banco [de sua preferência] no aplicativo e cadastrar a chave PIX. Mas tem que ser uma chave PIX com seu CPF [o mesmo que consta no CadÚnico]. Ele dando uma chave, vai receber", explicou Paula Sampaio, gerente do projeto "cashback" da Receita Federal.

Na hipótese de o beneficiário não tenha Poupança Social na Caixa e nem chave PIX cadastrada em nenhuma instituição financeira, a Receita informou que será aberta, em seu nome, uma Poupança Social para ele na Caixa - onde os valores serão depositados.

O governo federal lembra que o "cashback" que terá início a partir do próximo ano envolve apenas o seu tributo sobre o consumo, a Contribuição Sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), pois esse tributo começa a ser cobrado de forma efetiva no ano que vem.

Em 2027 e 2028, o Imposto Sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) dos estados e municípios será cobrado também, mas com alíquota pequena (de 0,1%). A partir de 2029, esse tributo aumentará, gradualmente, até 2032. A cobrança integral começa em 2033. Deste modo, a partir de 2029, também começará a haver "cashback" do imposto dos estados e municípios.

articles.title: 'Muita labuta': baiano relata história de luta até formar em medicina | G1
articles.standfirst: Otoniel Souza dos Santos reforça importância de programas sociais na sua formação. Para o médico recém-formado, os episódios de discriminação fortaleceram sua consciência política.
articles.summary: Otoniel Souza dos Santos reforça importância de programas sociais na sua formação. Para o médico recém-formado, os episódios de discriminação fortaleceram sua consciência política.
articles.body:
O baiano Otoniel Souza dos Santos se formou em Medicina na Universidade de São Paulo ( USP ), neste mês de novembro, após anos de dedicação aos estudos e de enfrentamento a preconceitos e limitações econômicas. Filho de um ajudante de pedreiro e de uma empregada doméstica, o jovem de 27 anos nasceu e foi criado em Euclides da Cunha , no sertão baiano, região marcada pela memória de Canudos e pela resistência de seu povo.

Em entrevista ao g1 , Otoniel contou que cresceu em meio a dificuldades financeiras, estudando em escolas públicas e contando com o apoio de programas sociais, além do esforço dos pais para garantir o sustento da família.

A trajetória, que o levou até uma das universidades mais prestigiadas da América Latina, foi construída com persistência, apoio familiar e acesso a políticas públicas que ajudaram a tornar possível a realização do sonho de se tornar médico.

"Sempre fui uma pessoa simples, nada de muito 'menino prodígio'. Minha história sempre foi marcada por muita labuta".

Jovem do sertão da Bahia celebra luta da família ao se formar em medicina pela USP — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Otoniel conta que a mãe trabalhava como empregada doméstica, "e não pelos eufemismos 'secretária do lar' ou 'funcionária do lar'". Já o pai era ajudante de pedreiro e fazia bicos. Ou seja, nem sempre conseguia trabalho.

Otoniel destaca que a melhoria das condições financeiras da família aconteceu de forma gradual. Segundo ele, até meados de 2015, a mãe chegou a receber apenas R$ 300 por mês como empregada doméstica. Depois, passou a trabalhar na equipe de limpeza de um hospital em Euclides da Cunha e alcançou a remuneração de um salário mínimo.

Nesse contexto, programas de transferência de renda, como o Bolsa Família, foram fundamentais para a sobrevivência da família.

"Acho importante falar sobre isso porque, quando divulgaram que eu tinha me formado em medicina, vi muitas pessoas defendendo a ideia de que tudo é mérito individual, sem reconhecer a importância das políticas públicas. Elas foram essenciais para que eu chegasse até aqui".

Embora sonhasse em cursar medicina desde a infância, Otoniel iniciou a vida acadêmica em outro caminho. Em 2016, ingressou no curso de Letras da Universidade do Estado da Bahia (Uneb), em razão das poucas opções de graduação disponíveis em sua cidade.

"A realidade que eu tinha em Euclides da Cunha era escolher entre Letras ou Agronomia. Como não queria Agronomia, optei por Letras, mesmo tendo medicina como objetivo", explicou.

Otoniel lembra que enfrentou preconceitos e dificuldades financeiras até a formatura — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A experiência, no entanto, não correspondeu às expectativas. Após algum tempo, ele decidiu trancar o curso e passou a trabalhar para viabilizar a mudança para São Paulo, onde teria mais oportunidades de preparação para os vestibulares.

Na grande metrópole, foi morar inicialmente na casa de familiares. A mãe enviava cerca de R$ 500 por mês para ajudá-lo com os custos básicos, e boa parte do valor era destinada ao transporte público. Nesse período, ele conquistou uma bolsa de estudos em um cursinho de Santo André .

A primeira experiência de moradia em São Paulo, contudo, foi difícil. Mais tarde, mudou-se para a casa da madrinha, no Jardim Fontalis, na zona norte da capital paulista, onde encontrou um ambiente mais acolhedor.

Depois de dois anos tentando uma vaga em medicina, decidiu abandonar os cursinhos presenciais e passou a estudar sozinho. Recebeu apoio de professoras que ofereceram aulas particulares de física e química, o que permitiu que alcançasse, pela primeira vez, a segunda fase da prova da Fuvest — principal forma de ingresso nos cursos de graduação da USP.

Com a chegada da pandemia da Covid-19, em 2020, retornou para Euclides da Cunha. Segundo ele, o período foi importante para se reconectar com as próprias origens e reorganizar a vida emocional.

"Foi em Euclides da Cunha que consegui me reconectar com coisas que tinha perdido ao longo daqueles anos. Voltar para casa me ajudou a entender que eu precisava estar mais tranquilo internamente para alcançar meus objetivos".

Ainda em 2020, voltou a avançar para a segunda fase da Fuvest e, enfim, conquistou a aprovação em medicina na USP. Também foi aprovado no curso em outras instituições, como a Universidade Federal de São Paulo ( Unifesp ).

Recém-formado em medicina, Otoniel destaca a importância de suas origens — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A aprovação, entretanto, não representou o fim das dificuldades. Segundo Otoniel, os desafios, naquele momento, eram de outra ordem.

Para ele, além dos obstáculos financeiros, existe uma dimensão simbólica relacionada à ocupação de espaços historicamente marcados pela desigualdade social.

"Estudar medicina na USP tem um significado muito forte. Venho de uma família trabalhadora do interior do Nordeste e passei a ocupar um espaço historicamente reservado para grupos privilegiados. Durante a graduação, vivi situações de preconceito que me fizeram refletir muito sobre a importância de democratizar esses ambientes".

Uma das experiências mais marcantes ocorreu ainda nos primeiros dias de aula, durante atividades remotas impostas pelo período pandêmico. Ele lembra que uma funcionária da universidade demonstrou incômodo por não reconhecer sobrenomes tradicionais entre os novos alunos.

"Ela perguntava onde estavam os filhos de médicos, os sobrenomes que conhecia. Aquilo me incomodou profundamente. Parecia que algumas pessoas ainda acreditavam que apenas determinados grupos pertencem àqueles espaços".

Apesar dos episódios de discriminação, Otoniel afirma que as situações fortaleceram sua consciência sobre a importância das políticas de inclusão e permanência estudantil.

Morador de uma das residências estudantis da USP, o médico relata que encontrou novas dificuldades relacionadas à manutenção financeira durante a graduação. Na época em que ingressou, o auxílio oferecido pela universidade era de R$ 500 por mês.

Por isso, passou a atuar no Centro Acadêmico (CA) da Faculdade de Medicina, onde participou de mobilizações para ampliar políticas de permanência. O grupo conseguiu aumentar o auxílio para R$ 700 e assegurar um complemento de R$ 300, elevando o benefício mensal para R$ 1 mil .

Além disso, Otoniel também trabalhou em cursos de atendimento a traumas realizados no Hospital das Clínicas da USP, o que ajudou a complementar sua renda.

Outra pauta defendida por ele em sua atuação no CA foi a ampliação do acesso à moradia estudantil. "Havia vagas ociosas em espaços destinados a residentes enquanto estudantes precisavam de alojamento. Lutamos para que essas vagas também pudessem ser utilizadas por alunos em situação de vulnerabilidade".

Ao longo dos seis anos de graduação, Otoniel diz que precisou lidar não apenas com as exigências da formação médica, mas também com desafios relacionados ao pertencimento e à saúde mental.

"Para quem vem da elite, já existem os desafios do curso de medicina. Para nós, existem outros além desses: manter-se financeiramente, encontrar pessoas com trajetórias parecidas e entender que aquele espaço também é seu".

Segundo ele, a distância da família e as diferenças sociais presentes na universidade tornaram a adaptação ainda mais difícil. "Quando você sai do interior para um grande centro sem estrutura financeira e longe dos pais, descobre o quanto isso pode ser doloroso".

Apesar da formação na USP, Otoniel rejeita a ideia de que sua trajetória seja resultado apenas de esforço individual.

"Meus pais foram fundamentais. Eles não tiveram as oportunidades educacionais que eu tive, mas sempre entenderam o valor da educação. Além disso, as políticas públicas foram decisivas para que eu chegasse até aqui".

O jovem espera que sua história inspire outros estudantes de cidades pequenas e regiões periféricas.

"Quero que outros meninos e meninas entendam que o lugar onde nasceram não determina até onde podem chegar. Minha história não é uma prova de sucesso individual. Ela mostra o que acontece quando existem oportunidades".

Recém-formado, Otoniel se prepara agora para as provas de residência médica. Inicialmente, cogitou seguir áreas como Cirurgia Geral e Ginecologia e Obstetrícia, especialidade que o conectava à história da avó materna, Neusa Maria de Jesus, que atuou como parteira durante muitos anos.

A escolha final, porém, foi pela Dermatologia. Para ele, a especialidade oferece qualidade de vida, mas também desperta interesse por revelar as desigualdades sociais estampadas na própria pele dos pacientes.

"Muita gente associa dermatologia apenas à estética, mas ela vai muito além disso. Nas expedições que participei pelo Pará, Rio Grande do Sul e Vale do Ribeira, percebi como doenças de pele também refletem desigualdades sociais e dificuldades de acesso à saúde", defende.

Enquanto aguarda a emissão do registro profissional, Otoniel pretende trabalhar e continuar estudando para a residência. No futuro, não descarta retornar por períodos mais longos a Euclides da Cunha.

articles.title: Ele gastou R$ 275 mil em Labubus e fez até dentes inspirados nos bonecos, mas e agora que a febre passou? | G1
articles.standfirst: Receita da Pop Mart, empresa por trás dos bonecos, caiu à medida que diminuiu o interesse pelos monstrinhos colecionáveis.
articles.summary: Receita da Pop Mart, empresa por trás dos bonecos, caiu à medida que diminuiu o interesse pelos monstrinhos colecionáveis.
articles.body:
Durante anos, os bonecos Labubu pareceram imparáveis. Colecionadores de todas as idades compravam avidamente as "caixas surpresa" — embalagens lacradas que continham esses monstrinhos peculiares —, pagando, muitas vezes, US$ 15 dólares (R$ 82,65) ou mais por unidade.

Aqueles que não conseguiam obter os personagens que desejavam estavam, frequentemente, dispostos a pagar valores muito mais altos no mercado de revenda.

O entusiasmo em torno dessas criaturas convenceu um superfã da Carolina do Norte, conhecido pelo nome de Ensito, a abandonar seu emprego na área de tecnologia em 2024 para se dedicar em tempo integral à criação de conteúdo sobre Labubus — chegando a viajar para lugares como Itália e Espanha em busca dos lançamentos mais recentes.

Ensito gastou mais de US$ 50 mil dólares, o equivalente a cerca de R$ 275 mil, para montar sua coleção de mais de 400 bonecos Labubu — um número que, disse ele à BBC, o deixa "envergonhado de mencionar".

Ensito chegou até a encomendar, com um dentista, uma prótese de dentes pontiagudos — no estilo dos personagens — para usar em eventos dedicados ao personagem.

Ensito posa com uma nova peça de sua coleção e exibe seus dentes personalizados, inspirados nos de um Labubu — Foto: Enesito/Arquivo pessoal

No entanto, nos últimos meses, as publicações sobre os monstrinhos peludos perderam força. "Antigamente, esses vídeos alcançavam 10 mil visualizações muito rapidamente; hoje, tenho dificuldade para conseguir o mesmo resultado", diz ele.

O foco de Ensito mudou para outras tendências, como a Hello Kitty e os brinquedos do tipo " squishy ", que são macios e maleáveis.

Isso é um sinal de que a febre que elevou o valor de mercado da Pop Mart — a empresa por trás da marca — a um patamar superior ao das gigantes americanas de brinquedos Hasbro e Mattel somadas pode estar perdendo o fôlego.

Analistas acreditam que a marca, sediada em Pequim, tem tido dificuldade em manter o interesse do público para além de um momento de viralização isolado.

Recentemente, a Pop Mart informou que suas vendas globais no trimestre encerrado em setembro caíram até 50% em comparação ao ano anterior.

A queda foi especialmente acentuada fora da China continental, com uma redução de ao menos 70% na receita obtida nos Estados Unidos.

Parte fundamental do apelo dos bonecos reside na dificuldade de encontrar alguns modelos de Labubu — Foto: Reuters

A Pop Mart não inventou as "caixas surpresa" ( blind boxes ), mas seus bonecos certamente ajudaram a popularizá-las ao redor do mundo.

Essa estratégia de vendas confere ao ato de colecionar um caráter "nostálgico", remetendo à sensação de abrir presentes na infância, explica a profissional de marketing Katelynn Carlson, que conheceu os Labubus pelas redes sociais e hoje possui 36 deles.

Um de seus primeiros Labubus foi um boneco raro, o que tornou a experiência "ainda mais empolgante", acrescenta ela.

A linha Labubu, lançada em 2019, tornou-se a de maior sucesso da Pop Mart. Os monstrinhos viraram referência de moda, sendo exibidos por celebridades como Kim Kardashian e Lisa, do grupo Blackpink.

Eles frequentemente atraíam longas filas e tornaram-se tão populares que a Pop Mart precisou retirar temporariamente os produtos de suas lojas no Reino Unido, após relatos de clientes que chegaram a brigar por eles. Um fã chegou a pagar mais de US$ 150 mil dólares por um Labubu gigante.

Parte fundamental do apelo reside na dificuldade de encontrar alguns modelos de Labubu. Os fãs compram, repetidamente, caixas surpresa na tentativa de conseguir a versão que desejam, afirma Samer El Hajjar, professor de marketing da Universidade Nacional de Singapura.

Katelynn Carlson acredita que as caixas surpresa, conhecidas como blind boxes, foram um dos principais elementos por trás da febre dos Labubu — Foto: Katelynn Carlson/Acervo pessoal

A Pop Mart conta hoje com 500 lojas em mais de 30 países e 2 mil máquinas de venda automática ao redor do mundo.

A empresa, que abriu seu capital em Hong Kong em 2020, está avaliada em quase US$ 24 bilhões e continua sendo uma das fabricantes de brinquedos mais valiosas do planeta , apesar de suas ações terem caído mais de 50% em relação ao pico registrado no ano passado.

Segundo El Hajjar, os investidores temem que o sucesso global da marca tenha sido apenas um fenômeno viral, e não um crescimento sustentável impulsionado pela fidelidade dos clientes a longo prazo.

Para Ensito, fica claro que a exclusividade dos bonecos ajudou a alimentar a febre em torno deles.

"Agora, a sensação é diferente. Entro em uma loja da Pop Mart e encontro uma série inteira de Labubus disponível", diz ele.

Ashley Dudarenok, da consultoria de pesquisa sobre o mercado chinês ChoZan, afirma que essa percepção de exclusividade diminuiu à medida que a Pop Mart aumentou a produção para atender à demanda.

A Pop Mart optou por não comentar as oscilações no preço de suas ações e não respondeu a perguntas da BBC sobre a queda nas vendas.

À medida que a febre por Labubus arrefece, alguns de seus concorrentes ganham popularidade.

Artigos colecionáveis ​​vendidos em embalagens surpresa — como os Sonny Angels (pequenos bonecos que lembram querubins, sem roupas) e as miniaturas Smiski, que brilham no escuro — têm esgotado rapidamente nas prateleiras.

Agora, também é possível encontrar personagens de My Little Pony e K-Pop Demon Hunters nesse formato de embalagem surpresa.

A Miniso, fundada na cidade de Guangzhou, no sul da China, comercializa uma variedade de personagens da Disney e da Marvel em embalagens surpresa, distribuídos por mais de oito mil lojas ao redor do mundo.

"Os consumidores não se preocupam muito com a origem da marca", afirmou Vincent Huang, executivo da Miniso, no início deste ano. "Eles estão mais voltados para a experiência de compra — o design, o custo-benefício e a diversão."

Pop Mart, criadora do Labubu, enfrenta a concorrência de marcas como a Miniso — Foto: Future Publishing via Getty Images

Especialistas afirmam que um dos maiores desafios da Pop Mart é criar personagens duradouros.

Esse é um aspecto em que a Sanrio — detentora da marca Hello Kitty e que registrou lucros recordes no ano encerrado em março — leva uma clara vantagem, sugere o analista Boustani.

A Pop Mart tem investido em estratégias para expandir sua marca, incluindo a criação de um parque temático em Pequim e o anúncio de um filme do personagem Labubu — seguindo, de acordo com alguns especialistas, os passos de gigantes do licenciamento como a Disney ou a Lego.

No entanto, ao contrário da Disney, que vende uma história antes de vender um brinquedo, a Pop Mart faz o caminho inverso, observa Dudarenok. "O verdadeiro teste para o próximo ano será saber se a Pop Mart consegue fazer com que as pessoas amem um personagem sem que ele precise ser exibido por uma celebridade."

Smiskis, bonequinhos que brilham no escuro, estão surgindo como concorrentes dos Labubus — Foto: Smith Collection/Gado via Getty Images

Após gastar quantias vultosas com os monstrinhos, o colecionador Ensito diz que agora questiona quanto tempo e dinheiro as pessoas investem em coleções a cada nova tendência que surge. "Sempre vai aparecer uma tendência a cada ano. Sempre vai ter algo que se torna muito popular."

Lawrence Yu, criador de conteúdo baseado em Melbourne, conta que, depois de dois anos correndo atrás dos Labubus, pretende ser "mais seletivo" antes de adicionar novos itens à sua coleção, que conta com cerca de 50 bonecos.

Seus vídeos de compras e de abertura de embalagens de Labubus, prática conhecida na internet como unboxing , chegavam a atingir um milhão de visualizações, mas o frenesi diminuiu, e hoje Yu raramente produz conteúdo sobre eles. "Acho, sem dúvida, que a tendência perdeu força. As pessoas ficam enlouquecidas, e depois o interesse simplesmente desaparece."

Clara Barbero, do Canadá, acredita que os Labubus já são uma "tendência morta" , mas continua atenta a lançamentos que possam ser interessantes.

"Estou sendo mais criteriosa com a minha coleção. Compro apenas o que acredito que continuarei gostando nos próximos anos, em vez de simplesmente adquirir a série mais recente que é lançada."

Lawrence Yu diz que gastou cerca de US$ 1,4 mil (R$ 7,7 mil) em Labubus — Foto: Lawrence Yu/Acervo pessoal

Mas os monstrinhos fofos ainda contam com fãs verdadeiramente dedicados.

Hedy Khaled, de Liverpool, na Inglaterra, diz que, embora o frenesi em torno dos bonecos esteja diminuindo, ela continua apegada à sua coleção de 70 estatuetas da Pop Mart.

Ela argumenta que existe uma diferença entre aqueles que seguem tendências e os "fãs de verdade"; portanto, a queda nas vendas não significa, necessariamente, que os Labubus perderam seu encanto.

Para Carlson, é a felicidade que os bonecos proporcionam — e não a tendência viral — que a motiva a continuar colecionando. Ela ainda se empolga com os novos lançamentos da Pop Mart, como a recente série de Labubus com temática de gatos, uma de suas favoritas.

"Acho que há algo de especial em acolher a nossa criança interior e aproveitar as coisas simplesmente porque elas nos fazem felizes."

A proposta, de autoria das vereadoras Tatiana Roque e Joyce Trindade, segue para sanção ou veto do prefeito.

O instituto articula o Plano Popular de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Cultural de Marechal Hermes, que reúne moradores, artistas, pesquisadores e lideranças locais. articles.title: Megaspeed Malaysian arm Speedmatrix under scanner
articles.summary: Kuala Lumpur: The spotlight is now on Malaysia as the fallout of the Nvidia spy scandal engulfs more companies and alleged South East Asia-based
articles.body: Kuala Lumpur: The spotlight is now on Malaysia as the fallout of the Nvidia spy scandal engulfs more companies and alleged South East Asia-based intermediaries. Fears of high-performance Nvidia chips finding their way to China through Malaysia, bypassing the US trade curbs, have swung the authorities here into action.Ministry of investment, trade and industry (MITI) has intensified the probe into Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd, in collaboration with Royal Malaysian Customs Department.Malaysia's home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said on Saturday that police had opened an investigation paper as early as April 2025 on allegations that Malaysian subsidiaries were used to circumvent US export restrictions on Nvidia AI chips.In a statement on Friday, MITI said emphatically that "it has never cleared Singapore-based Megaspeed or its Malaysian affiliate Speedmatrix.""Speedmatrix is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia. Any verification visits carried out by MITI at these facilities are part of its regular monitoring of the data center sector, and should not be taken to mean that a company has been cleared. Any suggestion otherwise is inaccurate," MITI stated.So what prompted MITI to take this stance when only a few days ago minister Johari Abdul Ghani said govt has not opened a formal inquiry into Speedmatrix as there was no evidence the firm broke the law by renting data centre space and using GPUs locally?Two things unfolded: Megaspeed's claims that inspections by US and Malaysian officials found no foul play, implying the company stayed in line, and second, industry sources said, the realisation that Malaysia's recent pivot to AI hardware, chip design and a strong data centre hub could possibly be hit if a rules-based ecosystem was missing from the narrative.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: US diesel prices retreat, fall below $6 per gallon for first time in two months
articles.summary: US diesel prices have falled below the $6 level for the first time in two months.
articles.body: US diesel prices have falled below the $6 level for the first time in two months. It has eased some of the pressure on consumers, farmers and businesses following a sharp increase triggered by disruptions to global oil supplies.The national average retail price fell to $5.998 per gallon on Saturday, according to fuel price tracker GasBuddy, cited by Reuters. The decline comes after diesel touched an all-time high of $6.519 on September 22, with prices briefly crossing $10 per gallon in California.The surge had become a wider economic concern because diesel is central to the transportation and freight industry. Higher fuel costs pushed up expenses for businesses and farmers, while adding to inflationary pressures on households. Fuel prices also became a major political issue, contributing to voter dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump's Republicans ahead of this month's midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep both houses of Congress.The earlier price rally was driven by supply disruptions linked to the US-Israeli war against Iran and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. Washington's efforts to contain the increase, including temporarily lifting federal taxes on red-dyed diesel, easing sanctions on Russian fuel and announcing an $8 billion support programme for farmers, offered limited relief.The latest retreat comes amid a combination of softer crude prices and seasonal changes in fuel consumption. Brent crude futures have dropped 18.5 per cent over the past two weeks, while demand for diesel typically weakens during autumn as travel slows and hurricane-related risks to Gulf Coast refineries decline.Refinery output is also recovering as scheduled maintenance is largely completed by November, Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy's head of petroleum analysis, said.The easing in fuel costs is not limited to diesel. Average US gasoline prices also fell below $4 per gallon this month for the first time since August 10, GasBuddy data showed.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: US air travel disruptions to persist until late on Sunday, FAA head says
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 14 (Reuters) - US air travel is not expected to return to normal schedules until late on Sunday, the head of the FAA said, as the aviation sy...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov 14 (Reuters) - US air travel is not expected to return to normal schedules until late on Sunday, the head of the FAA said, as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry.

As of 9:35 p.m. ET (0235 GMT), airlines on Saturday had ‌canceled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000, according to FlightAware, an aviation website. That followed about 9,200 flights canceled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after ‌the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications. FlightAware said 875 flights scheduled for Sunday were already canceled.

Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford said on Saturday that he expected airline operations to largely return to ​normal by late Sunday. He also apologized for the disruption, adding that the system remains stable.

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. It was the longest nationwide halt to air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001, and one of the single worst US travel days ever.

The issue prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday and federal agencies to scramble to determine if it was a cyberattack. But the problem was traced to FAA contractor L3Harris' installation of at least one new router at a remote ‌facility, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday.

"We're working to determine ⁠whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven't determined what the fault was," Duffy said at a press conference.

The Professional Aviation Safety Specialists, a union representing FAA safety employees, said the issue was isolated to two ⁠routers that were updated Friday. An official told Reuters it was believed the routers were in Arkansas and Texas.

An FAA official said the agency conducted a safety assessment before the work. The union said PASS-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop.

L3Harris said it took the issue seriously and is supporting the FAA in its investigation. Its shares last traded down about 4% after hours on ​Friday.

Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when air traffic control centers experienced instability in radar ​and communications systems. The router issue led to data overloading other communications centers, ‌officials said.

articles.title: 'Handshake' deals could fall through:  Musk flags supply chain risks for Nvidia after Jensen Huang's exit
articles.summary: Nvidia could lose some of its key supply chain agreements following Jensen Huang's departure, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has warned, pointing to the
articles.body: Nvidia could lose some of its key supply chain agreements following Jensen Huang's departure, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has warned, pointing to the personal nature of several business arrangements made during the former chief executive's tenure.Musk said Huang's ability to build and maintain relationships played an important role in securing deals for the chipmaker, with some agreements resting on personal assurances rather than written contracts.Taking to X on Saturday, Musk said, "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract."He further cautioned that Huang's absence could affect these arrangements. "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost," he added.Musk's comments also come amid efforts to bring Huang back to the top job. On Friday, he publicly supported a petition seeking the former CEO's reinstatement. "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too," Musk said in a post on X.His support for Huang had also been evident earlier when a social media user suggested that Musk hire the Nvidia co-founder. Responding to the suggestion, Musk said, "That would be an honor."Huang stepped down as Nvidia's president and chief executive officer amid growing scrutiny over reports of his alleged extramarital relationships.The New York Times reported that Huang allegedly had a relationship with Nvidia Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports to him. The newspaper based its report on accounts from five people who had worked at the company.The Wall Street Journal separately reported on Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected by some US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence services.After Huang's resignation, Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO as it begins the search for a permanent successor.Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and remained at its helm for more than three decades. During this period, he oversaw the company's growth into one of the world's leading suppliers of artificial intelligence chips.Musk's warning centres on the business relationships established during Huang's leadership, suggesting that his departure could have consequences beyond the change at the top. The Tesla CEO has specifically pointed to supply chain agreements that were built on his personal assurances rather than formal written commitments.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: India's life insurance sector set for 13-18% annual growth in premiums through FY29: Report
articles.summary: India's life insurance sector is expected to maintain healthy growth over the next three years, supported by rising demand for protection products,
articles.body: India's life insurance sector is expected to maintain healthy growth over the next three years, supported by rising demand for protection products, stronger traction in annuity and non-participating savings policies, and improving profitability, according to a research report by Centrum Broking.The brokerage expects private life insurers to record an annualised premium equivalent (APE) compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13-18% between FY26 and FY29, reflecting continued demand for insurance products and a gradual improvement in business mix.“We continue to remain optimistic on life insurance industry with a healthy Q2,” the report said, identifying a shift towards more profitable products and expanding value of new business (VNB) margins as key factors supporting the outlook.Protection and annuity products drive growthDuring the second quarter of FY27, APE growth among insurers ranged from 7% to 16%, while gross premium growth for private insurers stood at 8-16% year-on-year, according to the report.New business premium growth also remained encouraging, with insurers reporting increased traction in both individual and group insurance segments.One of the key trends highlighted by the brokerage was the industry's shift towards protection, non-participating savings and annuity products. Insurers have been reducing their dependence on unit-linked insurance plans (ULIPs), which are exposed to market fluctuations, while focusing on products that offer more stable margins and profitability.“Overall, annuity is emerging as a key growth driver, supported by demand for guaranteed returns and retirement solutions, while insurers increasingly shift towards protection and higher-margin products,” the report said.The changing product mix has also supported an improvement in VNB margins, which measure the profitability of new insurance business.During the first half of FY27, VNB margins expanded by 10-170 basis points year-on-year across private insurers. The report attributed the improvement to stronger protection business, a favourable product mix and operating leverage.Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) also recorded a 470-basis-point expansion in its VNB margin to 22.3%.Higher expenses and mixed persistency trends remain concernsDespite the growth in premiums and profitability, insurers continue to face operational challenges.Expense ratios increased across several private insurers in the second quarter of FY27, primarily because of higher operating costs. Persistency trends, which indicate the proportion of policies that remain active over time, were also mixed, with 13-month persistency declining across most insurers.On the regulatory front, insurers expressed confidence in their ability to comply with proposed norms. However, further clarity is expected after the final regulations are released.Centrum Broking said sustained growth in protection products and annuity offerings, along with expansion of distribution networks, would remain important drivers of the sector's business growth and profitability over the coming years.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: AI losing its shine? Why global investors could turn to India for their next big bet
articles.summary: As investors begin to question whether the AI frenzy is worth the money being poured into it, India could emerge as an attractive destination for global
articles.body: As investors begin to question whether the AI frenzy is worth the money being poured into it, India could emerge as an attractive destination for global funds. Heavy AI spending by US technology companies and concerns over returns may encourage fund managers to scout for opportunities beyond technology stocks, according to Jefferies.India could be among the biggest beneficiaries of this shift, the brokerage said in its latest GREED & fear investment strategy report."In emerging markets which GREED & fear knows more about, the obvious market to benefit from the reverse AI trade has been India."The report said more fund managers were now looking at investment options outside AI stocks, as doubts grow over whether the AI boom can continue."From an investment standpoint, the now widespread view that the AI thematic has peaked is leading to a growing desire to look at non-AI trades on the part of portfolio managers."Foreign investors bring money back to Dalal StreetSigns of this shift are already visible in foreign investment flows into Indian equities. Overseas investors have bought a net $7.2 billion worth of shares over three weeks, including a record $5.2 billion in the week ended November 6, Jefferies said.The buying comes after a period of heavy foreign selling. Net outflows from Indian equities stood at $32.4 billion since the beginning of 2026 and $51.2 billion since the beginning of 2025, measured over the respective periods.Jefferies said India's relatively attractive stock valuations and better-than-expected economic recovery were adding to its appeal."The other point about India is that valuations, relative to history, remain comparatively modest while the cyclical recovery in the economy this year has been better than expected."The Nifty was trading at 18.4 times its expected earnings over the next year, while the Nifty MidCap 100 was trading at 23.1 times its expected earnings.Machinery imports signal pickup in private investmentThe report also highlighted signs that private-sector investment is picking up. Machinery imports, an indicator of investment activity, more than doubled from $29 billion in FY21 to $62 billion in FY26. They rose further to $67 billion in the 12 months ending September 2026.Domestic investors have also continued to support the market through mutual fund investments. Equity mutual fund inflows stood at Rs 350 billion in October, taking the total for the first ten months of 2026 to Rs 3.9 trillion."India remains the most dynamic capital market in the world after the US," Jefferies said. However, the brokerage noted that the growing supply of equities had limited gains in benchmark indices.Why the AI investment story is facing questionsThe possible shift towards markets such as India comes as investors increasingly question the returns that large US technology companies are getting from their heavy AI spending.Jefferies said the median forecast return on invested capital for four major US technology companies had fallen from 21.7 per cent to 16.8 per cent for 2027. This decline comes even as their capital spending is expected to increase.The brokerage believes that growing concerns over AI investment returns could encourage global fund managers to diversify into other markets. India could benefit from this shift, backed by improving private-sector investment activity and continued inflows into domestic equity mutual funds.Money habits form by age 7.
