articles.title: Global economy to grow 2.8% in 2027 as AI spending, lower oil prices support outlook: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: The global economy is expected to maintain steady growth in 2027, supported by declining energy prices and continued investment in artificial intelligence
articles.body: The global economy is expected to maintain steady growth in 2027, supported by declining energy prices and continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI), although geopolitical tensions, fiscal pressures and uncertainty over technology spending could pose risks, according to a research report by Goldman Sachs.Global gross domestic product (GDP) is projected to expand by 2.8% in 2027, compared with an estimated 2.7% in 2026, said Jan Hatzius, chief economist and head of Goldman Sachs Research.The United States, Japan and the United Kingdom are expected to outperform consensus growth estimates, while South Korea and Taiwan are projected to benefit from continued strength in AI-related exports.“We expect another year of solid but unremarkable GDP growth in 2027, but several of the impulses that shaped global growth in 2026 will look different,” Hatzius said.Lower energy prices and AI spending to support growthA key factor behind the improved outlook is the expected moderation in energy prices. Goldman Sachs' commodity strategists expect Brent crude to fall to $78 per barrel by the end of 2027 as supply conditions in the Middle East normalise.The report said lower energy prices were expected to shift from being a drag on economic activity to providing modest support for global growth.AI investment is also expected to remain a significant contributor. Global nominal investment in AI is projected to rise to $1.8 trillion in 2027 from $1.1 trillion in 2026, driven largely by higher spending on hardware in the US.Goldman Sachs estimates that AI investment will add 0.4 percentage points to global GDP growth in 2027, with its contribution to US economic growth projected at 0.6 percentage points.“Even with the expected slowdown, the impact on GDP growth will be sizable,” Hatzius said.The scale of financing required for the AI infrastructure expansion has also come into focus. In a separate report, Goldman Sachs estimated that AI-related debt issuance across global syndicated credit markets had reached $687 billion year-to-date as of November 3.The report said the five major technology companies known as hyperscalers — Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle — had issued $296 billion in debt year-to-date, exceeding the bank's full-year forecast of $250 billion.Their financing obligations extend beyond direct borrowing. Goldman Sachs estimated that the five companies had $1.7 trillion in lease commitments and another $1.9 trillion in unconditional purchase commitments, excluding leases. Of the latter, $685 billion was due by the end of 2027.The bank cautioned that these commitments represented an additional demand on companies' cash resources. It also said market saturation was emerging as a key constraint on further AI-related borrowing.China growth outlook and risks to global economyAmong major economies, China is forecast to grow by 4.5% in 2027, slightly above the consensus estimate of 4.4%. However, weak domestic consumption and continued weakness in the property sector are expected to constrain domestic demand.Goldman Sachs said risks to global growth remained tilted to the downside, identifying a renewed escalation in Iran, widening fiscal deficits and lower-than-expected AI capital expenditure as potential sources of pressure.Inflation is expected to moderate as energy prices decline, potentially giving central banks room to move towards monetary policy easing later in 2027.The bank's outlook therefore points to continued global expansion, with lower energy costs and AI spending providing support, while geopolitical developments, fiscal conditions and the scale of future technology investment remain important risks.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Bad air, bigger bills: Air pollution drives health insurance claims up fourfold in 3 years
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Pollution is not just leaving people gasping for breath but also burning a bigger hole in their health insurance bills.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pollution is not just leaving people gasping for breath but also burning a bigger hole in their health insurance bills. Claims linked to pollution have surged more than fourfold in just three years, with working professionals bearing the biggest brunt, accounting for nearly six out of every 10 such claims, according to data released by insurance aggregator Policybazaar.The company's data showed that pollution-associated health insurance claims increased 4.34 times between FY23 and FY26. The rise was steady over the three years, with claims jumping 67% in FY24, another 70% in FY25 and 53% in FY26.Rohan Goel, Business Head, Health Insurance at Policybazaar, said, "India's rising pollution levels are increasingly reflected in its healthcare burden. Our health insurance data shows that pollution-associated claims have surged 4.3 times."Interestingly, respiratory illnesses were not the only major contributor to these claims. Cardiovascular conditions accounted for the largest share at 43.5%, while other respiratory infections made up 35%.Pneumonia accounted for 11.2% of claims, followed by bronchitis at 6%.Working professionals make up 59% of claimsThe 31-55 age group accounted for the largest portion of pollution-associated health insurance claims, at 59%. Senior citizens aged 55 and above were the second-largest group, contributing 31%.The remaining claims came from younger age groups. Young adults aged 21-30 accounted for 6.7%, while children below 20 years made up 3.7%.Goel said, "Working professionals aged 31-55 account for nearly 59% of claims, while senior citizens contribute another 31%."Delhi leads, but smaller cities are not far behindDelhi recorded the highest number of pollution-associated health insurance claims among cities. Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Hyderabad followed.However, the numbers were not concentrated only in major cities. Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities together accounted for 55% of the claims, showing that the trend extended beyond metropolitan centres.The timing of these claims also followed a seasonal pattern. In FY26, nearly 56% of all annual pollution-associated health insurance claims were recorded beween October and March, when air pollution levels typically worsen across several parts of the country.Total claim amount rises 4.5 timesThe increase in claims also came with a sharp rise in the overall amount paid out. Policybazaar's data showed that the total claim amount increased 4.5 times between FY23 and FY26. The average claim amount, meanwhile, continued to remain above FY23 levels.The data further showed that 48% of consumers living in highly polluted cities opted for higher health insurance coverage.Goel said, "These trends highlight the growing importance of preventive healthcare, timely medical attention and adequate health insurance coverage to manage the financial impact of unexpected medical needs."Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: India-Egypt trade has 'sky's the limit' potential, says Piyush Goyal; eyes bigger investments
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India and Egypt need to set their sights on a much bigger trade partnership, with greater two-way movement of goods, services and investments,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India and Egypt need to set their sights on a much bigger trade partnership, with greater two-way movement of goods, services and investments, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said, calling for exploring new business opportunities between the two countries.With bilateral trade currently at around $6.5 billion, Goyal said the existing numbers did not reflect the potential of the two economies. He was speaking at a community event hosted by the Indian Community Association in Egypt (ICAE) late last evening."For the size of our two economies, I believe it's just a beginning; it cannot be our destination; the sky's the limit," he said.India is looking beyond selling its products in the Egyptian market and wants to attract Egyptian goods and investments as well. Goyal said both countries needed to identify areas where they could benefit from each other's strengths, making trade a two-way exercise."We are looking at investment opportunities in Egypt; we are looking at marketing our goods and services...we are looking at Egyptian products coming to India and investments coming to India in areas of Egypt's strength, because ultimately trade has to be two-way. It has to be a win-win between the two nations," he said.The trade figures for 2025-26 show India's exports to Egypt at $3.87 billion, against imports of $2.60 billion. Meat and poultry products, petroleum products, organic chemicals, cotton and machinery are among India's main exports to the country. Crude petroleum, fertilisers, cotton and mineral products account for its major imports.Investment flows, however, remain limited. India received just $11.5 million in foreign direct investment from Egypt between April 2000 and June 2026.Goyal is visiting Egypt for two days with a 132-member business delegation. His schedule includes meetings with Egyptian leaders and business representatives to explore ways of increasing trade and investment between the two countries.India widens its trade networkGoyal also outlined India's broader approach to international trade, saying the government had placed it at the heart of the country's economic agenda. The focus, he said, was on opening up markets and securing preferential access for Indian goods and services, particularly in countries with which India has friendly relations."We are opening the doors for greater competition with the world, opening the doors of markets across the world for preferential access for Indian goods and services, particularly with our friendly countries. Towards that end, we have expanded our free trade agreements to many more developed nations," he added.India has implemented trade agreements with Mauritius, Australia, the UAE, Oman, the EFTA bloc, New Zealand and the UK over the past five years. An agreement with the European Union is scheduled to be signed next month.Negotiations are also under way with Canada, Chile, the South Africa-led South African Customs Union (SACU), the Brazil-led Mercosur grouping and the Russia-led Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU).Following these agreements, Indian goods will have preferential access to markets representing $85 trillion of the global GDP of $115 trillion.Looking to make it easier for companies in both countries to identify and pursue opportunities, Goyal proposed that the ICAE put together a business guide for Indian and Egyptian enterprises."Maybe you need to create a new 'Periplus' for businesses to engage between India and Egypt," he said.Periplus refers to an ancient guidebook or account of sea routes and trading ports.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: 76-year-old with Rs 35 lakh health cover denied Rs 3.87 lakh claim over wrong kidney disease entry corrected during admission; panel orders payout, 6% interest, Rs 50,000 compensation and Rs 35,000 costs
articles.summary: You have health insurance policies, but when you are hospitalised a wrong ailment is erroneously recorded in your charts, which the hospital later
articles.body: You have health insurance policies, but when you are hospitalised a wrong ailment is erroneously recorded in your charts, which the hospital later rectifies. But the insurance company rejects your claim for non-submission of mandatory documents, even though medical records had clarified the erroneous reference during the hospital admission. What do you do?In one such case, a 76-year-old woman had to pay Rs 3.87 lakh for her hospital treatment despite holding health insurance policies with a combined sum insured of Rs 35 lakh.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-VIII (Central), Delhi, held Nthe insurance company guilty of deficiency in service over its handling of the claim.In its order dated September 24, 2026, the commission found that the insurer continued to seek medical clarification despite records showing that the erroneous entry had been corrected during the same hospital admission.What the case is aboutA woman held two health insurance policies - the first provided a sum insured of Rs 10 lakh against a premium of Rs 96,673. The second carried a sum insured of Rs 25 lakh and involved an additional premium of Rs 54,499.According to the woman, she had disclosed her existing medical conditions, including diabetes, lipid disorders and hypertension, while obtaining the policies. She also stated that the insurer had conducted a pre-policy medical examination, whose report did not record any pre-existing disease relating to her heart or kidneys.In December 2023, she was admitted to the emergency department of a hospital in Delhi. The initial emergency assessment inadvertently recorded chronic kidney disease (CKD). The woman maintained that this entry was erroneous and was corrected through an addendum, before she was discharged.During her hospitalisation, a cashless claim request was submitted to the insurance company. The insurer sought additional medical records, investigation reports and clarifications. The woman stated that she supplied the requested information, including a treating doctor's certificate indicating that she had no history of CKD or coronary artery disease.The cashless request was nevertheless not approved, with the reason communicated being insufficiency or non-submission of the requisite documents. After being discharged, she paid the hospital bill of Rs 3.8 lakh herself and subsequently filed a reimbursement claim.The insurer acknowledged the reimbursement claim in January 2024, and sought hard copies of the original documents. It continued to request information over the following weeks. In February, it confirmed receipt of the physical documents and informed her that the claim was under hospital-level verification.Towards March-end, the insurer again sought an affidavit from the treating doctor confirming that there was no history of CKD.The woman argued that this was unnecessary because the hospital had already clarified the erroneous entry through the addendum and a medical certificate. According to her complaint, the treating doctor also explained that a separate affidavit from the emergency doctor would not be provided because the error had already been corrected in the medical record.The insurance company rejected the reimbursement claim by email in April 2024, citing non-submission of mandatory documents.The woman then approached the consumer commission, seeking reimbursement, interest, compensation and litigation expenses.The insurer did not file its written version within the statutory period. By an order dated May 29, 2025, the commission closed its right to file the written version and evidence. It subsequently considered the insurer's written arguments only on questions of law, not disputed factual matters that should have been presented through its written version and evidence.Why the court ruled in favour of the womanThe commission examined the medical records and correspondence between the parties, focusing on whether the insurer had acted reasonably in processing and rejecting the claim.It noted that the initial emergency assessment mentioned CKD, but the addendum correcting the entry had been issued during the same hospital admission. The treating doctor's clarification and other records were also available to the insurer.The commission observed: “The significance of the correction is that the alleged discrepancy was not discovered for the first time after the claim had been raised.”It further noted that the insurer had been informed about the correction and had received the treating doctor's clarification, yet continued to seek an affidavit addressing the same issue.The commission recognised that insurers can request documents to verify claims. However, it held that this right cannot justify repeated demands for material already supplied or documents that cannot reasonably be obtained in the circumstances.As the order stated: “However, such right cannot be exercised in a manner whereby the insured is repeatedly called upon to furnish documents which have already been supplied or documents which, in the circumstances, are not reasonably capable of being obtained.”The commission also observed that the insurer had not produced evidence establishing what essential information remained unavailable after the medical documents and clarifications had been furnished.Its February communication, confirming that the case was under hospital-level verification, indicated that the claim was being processed on the basis of the submitted documents.The order said: “In these circumstances, the subsequent rejection of the claim merely on the ground of non-submission of further documents, without satisfactorily establishing why the documents already supplied were insufficient for adjudication, amounts to an unreasonable handling of the insurance claim.”The commission also referred to the Supreme Court's decision in Manmohan Nanda v. United India Assurance Co. Ltd., noting the principle that an insurer that conducts a pre-policy medical assessment must assess the medical risk on the information available to it.Concluding that the claim had not been processed and decided fairly, reasonably and diligently, the commission held that the insurance company had committed deficiency in service.It stated: “The Commission is therefore of the considered view that the Opposite Party failed to process and decide the complainant’s claim in a fair, reasonable and diligent manner and thereby committed deficiency in service.”The commission directed the insurance company to pay the reimbursement amount, interest, compensation and litigation costs within 45 days of receiving the order.The commission directed the insurer to reimburse the hospital expenses of Rs 3,87,391, pay interest at 6% per annum from April 25, 2024, until realisation, and provide Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental agony, harassment and inconvenience. It also awarded Rs 35,000 towards litigation expenses.If it failed to comply with the monetary directions within that period, the principal reimbursement amount would carry interest at 9% per annum instead of 6%, calculated from April 25, 2024, until actual realisation.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Govt tightens procurement rules, mandates scrutiny of bids 30% below estimated cost
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The finance ministry has directed government agencies to scrutinise bids quoting prices more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost of a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The finance ministry has directed government agencies to scrutinise bids quoting prices more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost of a project or contract, tightening checks on unusually low offers to prevent compromises in quality and timely execution.The department of expenditure has defined such offers as Abnormally Low Bids (ALBs) and made it mandatory for procuring entities to examine them as potentially unviable. Agencies will have to seek written explanations from bidders when concerns arise over their ability to deliver the work at the quoted price."A bid quoting a price more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost shall mandatorily be examined as a potentially ALB," the department said in an office memorandum, as quoted by PTI.The bidder may be asked to provide a detailed price analysis in relation to the scope of work specified in the tender document. The procuring agency will assess whether the quoted amount is sufficient to meet the contract requirements.However, the new threshold does not mean that every bid priced more than 30 per cent below the estimate will be rejected. The department clarified that the threshold would not be grounds for "automatic rejection" and that bidders would be given an opportunity to explain how they intend to execute the contract at the offered price.A bid may be rejected if the bidder fails to adequately demonstrate its ability to complete the work at the quoted rate. In such cases, the agency can consider the next higher bidder, provided its price is found reasonable.The move addresses a gap in earlier procurement rules, which did not prescribe a fixed numerical threshold for identifying abnormally low bids. Government agencies largely relied on their own assessment of whether an unusually low quotation posed a risk to the execution of a contract.The department has also advised procuring entities to frame tender specifications carefully to guard against such bids. The revised framework is intended to bring greater uniformity and transparency to the process while allowing genuine price competition.Government agencies invite bids from companies and contractors through a tender process to procure goods, services or carry out projects. Interested bidders submit their technical proposals and price quotations, which are evaluated against the conditions specified in the tender. While a lower price can make a bid more competitive, an unusually low quote may raise questions about whether the bidder can meet the required quality standards and complete the contract within the agreed cost.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Pact on South China Sea code of conduct unlikely, as ASEAN leaders gather
articles.summary: Finishing negotiations for disputed South China Sea agreement will be a ‘tall order’, analysts say.
articles.body:
A long-awaited pact between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China for a “code of conduct” in the disputed South China Sea is unlikely to materialise during the regional bloc’s annual gathering of leaders in Manila this week, analysts and officials say.

The agreement would aim to manage tensions and prevent conflict at sea. But talks have dragged on for more than 20 years. In 2023, foreign ministers agreed to work towards finalising the accord within three years.

That deadline fell on 2026 – the year the Philippines took its turn as chair of ASEAN. Under its leadership, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said negotiators have met at least once a month.

But they have fallen short of arriving at a consensus ahead of the summit.

“I just want to say that at this point in time, 80 percent of the document itself is finished,” DFA Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro said on Saturday, adding that there are some ‘salient’ points that still need to be ironed out.

She has previously said that geographical scope is one of the contentious issues. Beijing insists it has jurisdiction over nearly the entire South China Sea despite a 2016 international ruling invalidating that claim.

The Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia also have overlapping territorial claims.

The Philippines would also like the accord to respect the rights of countries outside the region, according to DFA spokesman Dominic Xavier Imperial. Half of the world’s merchant ships pass through the South China Sea.

But the country may be caught between a rock and a hard place.

“You can’t win it because if you get a good document, you’ll be accused of railroading or it would come across as self-serving. But if it’s a bad document, the Marcos Jr administration will be seen as a weak government,” Aries Arugay, a political scientist at the University of the Philippines, said.

China has consistently accused the United States and its allies, who regularly conduct freedom of navigation operations with the Philippines, of interference.

Tensions between Manila and Beijing have escalated since Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr took office in 2022. The China Coast Guard has repeatedly deployed water cannon against Philippine vessels and maritime confrontations have resulted in collisions and, on one occasion, a Filipino soldier losing a finger.

In recent weeks, the two countries have been engaged in a war of words.

In September, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro’s public response to a handwritten note rejecting the 2016 South China Sea ruling – reportedly from Beijing’s military attache in Seoul – went viral.

“Perhaps basic decency and behaviour is what China needs to do,” Teodoro, who has been barred from entering China, said.

A month later, Beijing’s ambassador to Manila, Jing Quan, told reporters that if China wanted to use force, “we may easily win. But no, we will not choose force. We love peace”. The statement was made in response to a question about Teodoro calling China a “troublemaker”, but which Marcos said “sounded like a threat”.

What followed was a barrage of social media posts by Philippine officials criticising Jing, with the Chinese embassy replying in kind. Senators called for the expulsion of the Chinese envoy.

And, in late October, China accused Teodoro of a late invitation to the ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting in Cebu. Without ample time to prepare, it said it could only send its Manila-based defence attache.

“When that happened, I think the concern, especially on the part of the DFA, was, ‘We don’t want China not sending their premier. It would not look good on us as a host country,’” Lucio Pitlo, past president of the Philippine Association for Chinese Studies, said.

With just days before world leaders were due to arrive in Manila, diplomats from both sides stepped in.

In a phone call, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Lazaro, his Philippine counterpart, to rein in politicians.

“The Philippines should strengthen restraint over the relevant individuals and send a rational and unified voice on its policy toward China,” Wang said in a statement released by the Chinese embassy in Manila.

Lazaro described the conversation as having been “frank and constructive”.

However, the DFA followed up with a statement saying it found public commentary by certain government officials “regrettable”.

“Whatever personal convictions public officials may hold, their public platforms carry institutional responsibilities,” it said. “They may not pursue preferred approaches toward China, or any other international partner, without regard for the consequences on the government’s overall policy.”

Some analysts say the spat has further exposed division within the Marcos administration.

“They’re airing dirty laundry out there. It doesn’t communicate coherence. It doesn’t project a unified stance. This could have been an internal memo,” Arugay said.

But Pitlo said the last-ditch diplomatic effort had achieved its objective. Chinese Premier Li Qiang is now attending the ASEAN Leaders’ Summit in Manila.

Despite this, Pitlo shares pessimism about leaders reaching a conclusion to negotiations for a code of conduct in the South China Sea.

“I think with all the concerns about trade protectionism, the disruption in supply chains, economic issues will be very high in the agenda. I think it will be a tall order to get the code of conduct done.”

articles.title: FPIs pump Rs 84,290 crore into Indian equities in November after two months of outflows
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) returned to Indian equities in November, pumping in Rs 84,290 crore in the first 13 days of the month after
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) returned to Indian equities in November, pumping in Rs 84,290 crore in the first 13 days of the month after two consecutive months of net selling. The sharp reversal in foreign flows comes amid a global sell-off in artificial intelligence-linked stocks, falling crude oil prices and renewed interest in select large-cap Indian shares.FPIs made net investments during nine trading sessions between November 2 and 13, according to data from depositories. The latest buying has also narrowed their cumulative net withdrawals from Indian equities in 2026 to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore, from nearly Rs 3 lakh crore a few weeks ago.The return of foreign money follows net outflows of Rs 35,861 crore in September and Rs 34,843 crore in October, reflecting the pressure Indian equities faced from overseas investors in the preceding months.However, market experts caution that the latest buying may not signal a sustained return of foreign investors."November's foreign buying is a sharp tactical turn, not yet a structural return. Falling crude and money rotating out of the crowded Asian AI trade have pushed FPIs to close an extreme underweight on India, and most of that buying has gone into index heavyweights," said Vedant Gupte, co-founder and CEO of investment platform Trackk, as quoted by PTI.He added that foreign investors had recovered only a small portion of their withdrawals this year, while domestic institutional investors were using the market rally to book profits.Foreign portfolio investors are overseas individuals, institutions or funds that invest in financial assets such as shares and bonds in another country. Unlike foreign direct investors, they generally do not seek management control of the companies they invest in. Their buying and selling activity can influence stock prices, market liquidity and the flow of foreign capital into an economy.Why are foreign investors returning to Indian markets?The sell-off in global AI-linked stocks has encouraged investors to look beyond technology-heavy markets and explore opportunities elsewhere, said Rohan Goyal, investment research analyst at MIRA Money.A decline in crude oil prices has also improved the investment outlook for India, which imports a large share of its oil requirements. Brent crude fell around 13 per cent in the first week of November to nearly $97 per barrel. Easing geopolitical concerns, attractive valuations in select large-cap stocks and better visibility on domestic corporate earnings have further supported foreign buying, Goyal said.The inflows have helped the benchmark Nifty cross the 25,000-mark. Financials, telecom, capital goods, pharmaceuticals and automobile stocks have seen strong buying, while some power-related shares have gained on the back of robust earnings, said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments.He also attributed part of the market rally to short-covering in frontline large-cap stocks, particularly select leading banking shares.What should investors watch next?The direction of foreign flows and the sustainability of the market rally will depend on several domestic and global factors. Markets will track minutes of the US Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting, crude oil prices amid tensions involving Iran and Gulf countries, movements in the rupee and expectations around a possible RBI rate hike next week.The remaining second-quarter corporate earnings announcements, broader market participation and the Nifty's ability to hold above 25,000 will also influence sentiment. Developments in the global unwinding of the AI trade will remain another key factor, said Dheeraj Gaur, chief investment strategy officer at Choice Wealth.In the debt market, foreign investors invested Rs 7,815 crore through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) and Rs 1,167 crore through the general route. They withdrew Rs 702 crore through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR).Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: 'Preferential trade access already agreed': Piyush Goyal's big update on India-US trade deal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India has secured an agreement with the United States to receive preferential market access for its goods, with lower import duties than
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has secured an agreement with the United States to receive preferential market access for its goods, with lower import duties than competing countries, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday.Goyal said the understanding was reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump when the two countries announced a broad framework for their bilateral trade agreement (BTA). Negotiations are currently underway to finalise the first phase of the deal."This was already agreed between the leaders - President (Donald) Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi when they announced that we have both come to a broad framework agreement a few months ago and it has been acknowledged that India will get preferential trade access in the US with lower duties than our competitor countries," Goyal told reporters in Cairo.The minister is on a two-day visit to Egypt to discuss ways to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries.India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement in February. The deal was expected to be signed earlier, but changes in the US tariff structure have led to further negotiations.An official had recently said that Washington had assured New Delhi of a comparative tariff advantage for Indian goods under the proposed agreement. Both sides are working to conclude the first tranche by the end of the current financial year."We will have to see how the tariff framework unfolds. We are working towards closing the first tranche by the end of this financial year. Talks are going for the first tranche and the broader BTA," the official said last week.The extent of the tariff advantage for Indian goods will depend on the final framework agreed upon by the two countries.The negotiations have also been affected by changes in US trade policy after the Supreme Court struck down President Trump's reciprocal tariffs, which had formed the basis of the earlier discussions. Washington is now exploring alternative mechanisms under provisions of the Trade Act to put a new tariff framework in place.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: The systems used to keep America flying are ancient. That makes fixing the problem that much more difficult
articles.summary: In some ways, America’s air traffic control system performs far better than one might think — even if it would be tough to convince the more than one million passengers who had their travel plans upended in recent days.
articles.body: In some ways, America’s air traffic control system performs far better than one might think — even if it would be tough to convince the more than one million passengers who had their travel plans upended in recent days. It handles a huge airspace and more than 45,000 flights a day. Yet, failures are exceedingly rare, even when its antiquated equipment breaks down. The current system uses strips of paper with the names of flights on them to be handed off from one controller to another, floppy computer discs and copper wire to handle communications for nearly a third of the system. Experts say that fixing a system this large is a tall order, partly because the current system is so old. “If you own a car for 30 years, it’s going to be increasingly difficult as the car gets older to find the replacement parts you need to keep it in operating condition. The same is true of any kind of technology serving any kind of industry,” said Henry Harteveldt, president of Atmosphere Research Group and a travel industry analyst. “There are many parts of airline and aviation technology that are no longer fit due to their age.” And Friday afternoon, the painstaking efforts to keep that antiquated air traffic control system functioning caught up with the Federal Aviation Administration and the more than one million on-board and would-be passengers. The problems arose when a contractor was working to replace some of the copper wire with fiber optics. “That new equipment, new technology just was overwhelming the older system,” said Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin. “The patchwork doesn’t work.” The part of the air traffic control system that monitors and communicates with planes at their cruising altitude was no longer reliable enough to keep those planes in the air or allow new planes to take off. So, the FAA ordered a rare systemwide “ground stop,” leading to 9,200 canceled flights, according to tracking service FlightAware. And even though the ground stop was lifted just after 8 p.m. ET on Friday, many flights could not be started at that point due to staffing issues or the lack of planes being in the right city. So another 6,200 were canceled on Saturday. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the problem is coming up with a modern system while keeping the current antiquated system up and running. “I don’t want to lie to anybody,” he said Friday night at the same press conference. “What we’re doing is hard, and it hasn’t happened in the past because it is hard. But I’ll tell you, by doing nothing, you inject way more risk into the system. “We use 1980s technology, 1990s software, to use 1970s radar that we don’t make parts for anymore,” he said. Earlier problems from old systems Friday’s ground stop wasn’t the first time the aging infrastructure has disrupted travel. Communication issues with the air traffic control systems directing flights around heavily trafficked Newark Liberty Airport in May 2025 caused the FAA to limit the number of flights and resulted in air traffic controllers becoming so stressed from not being able to communicate with planes that some workers took trauma leave, causing a staffing shortage to worsen. In a similar situation to Friday’s grounding of flights, in January 2023, the system used to notify pilots of their route’s conditions went down, grounding all flights. Airlines also have old technology It’s not just the FAA that copes with older technology. Even the actual airlines use outdated tools. In July 2024, an automatic update from cybersecurity software provider CrowdStrike caused massive problems on Windows computers, which impacted companies all around the world and required a restart of computers. But no company had a harder time restarting normal operations than Delta Air Lines, which had greater problems bringing its crew-tracking software back online, leaving it unable to staff airplanes. A massive problem at Southwest Airlines during the 2022 year-end holidays resulted in 16,700 canceled flights, millions of passengers scrambling to complete their holiday travel and costing the airline at least $1 billion. Much of it was due to problems with its own antiquated crew scheduling system, which required phone calls between the airline and crew members rather than online check-ins — a system that would make it impossible for the airline to find the crews it needed to staff flights. Harteveldt, the travel analyst, said Southwest has spent at least $1.3 billion since then upgrading its technology, hardware, software and communications networks. “We have a much better understanding of our crew network and are able to work in real time to adjust to unexpected circumstances,” Southwest said Saturday in response to a question about its upgrades. Hesitance to pay for new tech Airlines can be reluctant to fund back-office technology upgrades when they can instead spend on ways to attract more passengers, such as better Wi-Fi, newer planes and upgraded airport lounges, said Harteveldt. “They are risk-averse, and so they want to be sure that whatever technology they do end up investing in is a technology that will be useful long term to the airline,” he said. “That’s another reason why airlines tend to be technology laggards. They also just don’t have the profit margins, even in the best of years, to allocate large sums to technology upgrades.” The FAA’s problems are strictly political: it needs Congress to approve funding. Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion for air traffic control upgrades, and before Friday, Duffy had asked for another $30 billion. On Friday night, he said the agency now needs $50 billion. It’s possible the mess at the nation’s airports on Friday night will help win support for that greater Congressional spending. But the problems have existed for years. And even if the FAA has unlimited funds, it’s clear from the problems created by Friday’s attempted upgrade of existing systems that it won’t be repeated in the future. “Is this exact thing going to happen again? I don’t know,” Duffy said. “I think there’s no better time than the present to actually give us the money and let us finish.”

articles.title: Air India resumes non-stop New York, Newark flights after easing of airspace curbs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Air India has resumed non-stop flights from Delhi and Mumbai to New York and Newark after restrictions on airspace were eased, reducing travel
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Air India has resumed non-stop flights from Delhi and Mumbai to New York and Newark after restrictions on airspace were eased, reducing travel time on the routes by up to five hours.The airline said on Sunday that all four India-US routes were now operating without a technical stopover. The services had earlier included a halt in Rome for refuelling because of airspace restrictions across parts of the Middle East and the closure of Pakistani airspace.Air India began operating the non-stop services in the first week of November, using Iraqi airspace, sources told PTI."With airspace restrictions eased, Air India has now resumed non-stop operations on all four India-New York routes," the airline said.With the resumption of direct operations, travel time on flights from Delhi and Mumbai to New York and Newark has fallen to around 17 hours from nearly 22 hours earlier, the airline said.Air India operates one daily flight from Delhi to New York and four weekly services to Newark, all using Airbus A350-900 aircraft.From Mumbai, the airline operates daily flights to New York and three weekly services to Newark using Boeing 777-300ER aircraft.The closure of Pakistani airspace and restrictions across parts of the Middle East amid regional conflicts had disrupted flight routes between India and North America.As a result, Air India's flights from Delhi and Mumbai to John F Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in New York and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) had to make a technical stop in Rome for refuelling. Earlier, longer routes through Jordan and Egypt had also increased flying time.Last month, a senior airline official said the restrictions, particularly those linked to the West Asia crisis, had significantly affected operations, with the impact being worse than the previous year."The more airspaces are closed, the more southwards flights have to go... the more southwards flights have to go, the more the fuel bill. So, it (airspace curbs) is worse than what we had last year," the official had said.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Should you buy Nvidia stock right now?
articles.summary: Some guideposts to watch from Nvidia before hitting the buy button on its bruised stock.
articles.body:
It has been a week to remember in the investing world.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) ousting of legendary founder Jensen Huang was in no way on my bingo card coming into 2026. Huang's fall from C-suite grace is the most stunning I have ever seen and may ever see again in my career.

People in the tech world I have talked to are simply stunned at the out-of-the-blue turn of events. They are very angry with Jensen and, in the same breath, are worried about the lasting damage to the company he founded in 1993.

Many have wondered if they will be forced to diversify from Nvidia chips should the company lose its design prowess. That shift could bring massive changes to the supply chain feeding the AI infrastructure boom.

Some have told me the outlook for neoclouds such as CoreWeave ( CRWV ) is riskier in a world without Huang at the helm — the bank of Jensen was a great backstop.

Against this backdrop, of course, Nvidia's stock has tanked . The Jensen premium is evaporating, and it's hard to envision where the company will be 18 to 24 months from now in terms of its vital product roadmap.

Does the company even hold its splashy GTC events in 2027? Why bother — they have always been Jensen shows. It's probably best to cancel them so a new CEO can review the business and decide whether to bring them back in 2028.

"I mean, Jensen has been probably the most prominent CEO over the last couple of years. Or, you know, in the top couple. So I don't know what this change portends. It's just, it's change," Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman told me at Yahoo Finance Invest . "Nvidia is a very important company. So look, I am watching along with everybody else where this goes."

You are probably wondering if you should buy Nvidia stock right now. I am not going to say whether you should buy, sell, or hold it. That's not my job anymore.

But I will give you several things you want to start seeing from Nvidia before hitting the buy button on its bruised stock. Use these as guideposts — not all of them have to happen at once.

A story floating is that the permanent CEO search is down to three or fewer candidates, and that it will be an external hire. I just don't trust the insides of Nvidia's culture at the moment.

That same story saying the permanent CEO search is down to three or fewer very big names in the tech industry. I truly believe this is a moment where Nvidia should give former Apple ( AAPL ) CEO Tim Cook whatever he wants to take the job for the next two to three years.

The board comes back from its investigation and concludes 1) Jensen didn't have more affairs with direct reports (this matters, I think, because you could lose key talent if he did have more affairs with direct reports); and 2) Jensen didn't divulge company secrets to the reported Chinese spy he was having an affair with.

Interim CEO Colette Kress comes out on the earnings call next week with clear guidance on how much stock Nvidia plans to buy in the current quarter under its historic new $150 buyback authorization. She also overshares on Nvidia's long-term product roadmap.

articles.title: Nvidia's first post-Jensen earnings and Anthropic's IPO: What to watch this week
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO and continued fallout at Nvidia will lead the news cycle on Wall Street this week.
articles.body:
As if last week couldn't have gotten any busier, the biggest business story of the year rocked investors as scandal embroiled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and forced the "godfather of AI" to step aside, a proposition that looked unthinkable only days earlier.

But lest we forget, the news cycle goes on, and this week brings its own major headline: Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO, expected to price on Wednesday and trade on Thursday.

As the first pure-play generative AI company to come to market, investors will be paying close attention to every angle.

Markets will go into a fresh week continuing the feeling of post-election whiplash, though perhaps for different AI-based reasons. But incredibly, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) is almost exactly where it was before the election results as, once again, major headlines and crosscurrents have more or less canceled each other out.

Lots of action, little motion, broadly speaking.

Anthropic will dominate headlines this week, but that doesn't mean we've got an empty calendar of other news happening. On the earnings front, Nvidia ( NVDA ) (of all companies, what timing!) will report its quarterly results on Tuesday, with interim CEO Colette Kress set to helm the management call after the sudden call-up.

It's also a huge week for retail. We've got big box stores Target ( TGT ) on Wednesday, and Walmart ( WMT ) and Ross Stores ( ROST ) on Thursday, with BJ's Wholesale Club ( BJ ) rounding out the group on Friday for a check on consumer spending and outlook.

In the tech space, Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) and Bending Spoons ( BSP ) will report on Wednesday and Friday, respectively. Two of China's largest companies, Baidu ( BIDU ) and Alibaba ( BABA ), will give their own results on Monday and Thursday, respectively.

On the economic data calendar, the key readouts will be retail sales data on Tuesday and the University of Michigan's twice-monthly readout on consumer sentiment on Friday.

An AI world without Jensen looks to what's next

In a move practically unthinkable only a week ago, Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday as CEO of Nvidia, the world's leading chipmaker and, up until recently, the market's most valuable company.

The headlines trickled in slowly at first before a deluge of reports revealed affairs first with a Chinese national suspected by US intelligence to be a spy for Beijing — and then with two Nvidia employees.

While the board looks for a permanent replacement, CFO Colette Kress has taken up the mantle as interim CEO, with tons of open questions facing the company Huang founded more than 30 years ago.

articles.title: Jensen Huang resigned in disgrace from Nvidia. Many in Silicon Valley are still showering him with support
articles.summary: Following his departure, current and former staff responded with tributes on social media.
articles.body: Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia was marked by corporate scandal, but many of his own former employees and colleagues across Silicon Valley are coming out in droves to express support for the man they believe to be a legend. Huang resigned on Thursday after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with at least one subordinate. He had already been under scrutiny after reports of an affair with another woman, who was described by US officials as a potential Chinese intelligence asset. Huang was so integral to Nvidia’s brand that his image — with signature black leather jacket — was often turned into marketing material, including an AI-powered hologram at the company’s annual conference, known as GTC. Known for its low turnover and flat corporate structure, with Huang managing over 50 direct reports and responding to messages at all hours, Nvidia fostered deep employee loyalty. Following his departure, current and former staff responded with tributes on social media. Edward Liu, a director and distinguished scientist who started as an intern at the company, called it “a heartbreaking day,” in a post on X, praising Huang as an inspiring leader who taught them to “reason from first principles.” Engineer Fei Peng went even further, writing that Huang’s departure “has killed NVIDIA’s soul.” Others, like senior research scientist Gavin Woolery, openly suggested ulterior motives and suspicions about his ousting. Woolery posted on X that he felt Huang’s ousting came too quickly before all the information emerged. “Everyone deserves a fair trial. It’s possible he has made mistakes, I’m not sure they were ill-intentioned ones, but in either case we should know the whole truth before we judge,” Woolery said. Other employees expressed support for Nvidia’s interim leader, CFO Colette Kress. “I am grief-stricken that Jensen is no longer with NVIDIA,” posted Bryan Catanzaro, Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research. “At the same time, I fully support NVIDIA’s board and have confidence in their decisions. I’ve worked with Colette for years and know her as an extraordinary leader. She has my full support.” Beyond Nvidia’s walls, Huang’s influence was felt across the broader tech ecosystem. Often called the “central bank” of the booming AI industry, Nvidia not only supplied the hardware powering the technology but also financed much of the sector through investments and partnerships, with Huang serving as its biggest cheerleader. That has led to criticism and fears of “circular financing,” in which Nvidia invests in companies that fuel its own growth when those businesses turn around and use Nvidia capital to purchase Nvidia products. Exolabs founder Alex Cheema wrote about cold emailing Huang in June about an idea to make local AI much faster on Nvidia hardware. Huang responded in seven minutes and “approved a war room for us to work on this at NVIDIA HQ,” Cheema wrote. Cheema pointed to Huang’s long-time support and promotion of open-source technology — software or hardware built on publicly accessible source code that anyone can freely inspect, modify and distribute. Most of the major AI models, like ChatGPT and Claude, run on closed-source systems. “I don’t believe Jensen is replaceable, he’s a 1 of 1 human, but I hope NVIDIA will continue to aggressively support Open Source AI and Local AI, and continue to take bets on small startups with crazy ideas,” Cheema said. Huang also found support among his peers — some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley and venture capital, including his longtime friend and business partner, Elon Musk. Even before Huang was ousted, Musk posted that it would be “an honor” to hire Huang after another user on X implored him to do so. “A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too,” Musk later posted on Friday after Huang’s resignation. “Dark, dark day. Horrible decision for the U.S. and the western world,” Andreessen Horowitz general partner Martin Casado posted on X. The firm’s account also posted a clip from a movie about Michael Jordan, along with the quote: “ You’re gonna be remembered forever because some things are eternal.” Even those who have criticized his actions, like Sequoia Capital’s Shaun MaGuire, who called Huang’s actions a “dumb mistake” and “bad for America,” often come with a dose of praise. “He made huge mistakes with his infidelity, which is tragic for his family and NVDA. But simultaneously he will leave a huge void, with the loss of a: technical, aggressive, founder-CEO,” MaGuire wrote on X.

articles.title: As students rely on AI in college applications, admissions offices scramble to keep up
articles.summary: The college admissions essay is in a very weird place. It’s impossible to say just how many of them are now written by AI, but at this point, experts agree that it’s a lot of them. And while colleges generally frown upon that practice, they’re using AI to evaluate the essays, too.
articles.body: The college admissions essay is in a very weird place. It’s impossible to say just how many of them are now written by AI, but at this point, experts agree that it’s a lot of them. And while colleges generally frown upon that practice, they’re using AI to evaluate the essays, too. It’s all adding up to a scramble to stay ahead over the future of who gets to go to the university of their choice. Kate Gilbertson, who graduated from UC Berkeley in 2025 and edits college applications full time, said that lately she’s received a lot of drafts that don’t have the usual quirks of teenage writing. “Those little moments of flaw tell me that this is still a 17-year-old’s writing, right?” Gilbertson said. It’s not just essays. Though ChatGPT has been out for just four years, AI has already reshaped the entire college admissions process from top to bottom. Now, as the January 1 deadline for the Common App approaches, more and more high schoolers are using AI in their college applications and even turning to chatbots instead of college counselors, who often charge thousands of dollars for their services. Meanwhile, colleges are rushing to update their AI usage guidelines and rethink the future of the essay. Yet they are also testing out AI evaluations of their own to help sift through thousands, if not tens of thousands, of applications. Students, meanwhile, see an obvious double standard: If some universities are using AI to grade essays, why can’t I? If everyone is using AI to get ahead, why should I get left behind? Different rules for different schools Admissions offices around the country are rushing to figure out guidelines for AI use in applications, and each one looks a little bit different. But “students are moving faster than admissions offices” when it comes to AI, Ashley Pallie, California Institute of Technology’s dean of undergraduate admissions, said. CalTech, which is at the forefront of AI research, takes a nuanced approach. Its admissions office whittled down thousands of applicants to less than 450 admitted students last year. For Pallie, the process is much more art than science. She said an AI bot couldn’t replace the job of professional essay readers anytime soon. While “replacing your unique voice and tone with AI generated content” is unethical, the school said that “generating questions or exercises to help kick start the brainstorming process” is okay. The University of Pennsylvania warned against AI usage for letters of recommendation written by counselors and teachers. Colleges are also differing in how they grade essays, with some using AI tools themselves. “You actually can’t develop the perfect formula that’s going to choose the right students for you. You do need humans who are reading the humans who submitted their application,” Pallie said. However, CalTech does use an AI that reads students’ scientific research and asks them questions that faculty later views. Major public universities like Virginia Tech, which received a record 57,6222 first-year applications for 2025, are testing out AI to keep up with the mass application volume. That experimentation hasn’t always worked. UNC-Chapel Hill reversed its decision to auto-score application essays based on writing quality. The student newspaper reported that a university spokesperson said that “the widespread use of AI-assisted writing tools was the factor diminishing the usefulness of AI essay ratings.” Is this the end of the college essay? More colleges are dropping supplemental essays altogether for this application cycle. Tulane said that it is no longer requiring a “Why Tulane?” essay. While spokesperson Michael Strecker told CNN the essay hasn’t been that important in the selection process in recent years, he “can confirm that concerns about AI did play a role in this decision.” Sophie Sajnani, who graduated college in 2025, founded a boutique college consulting firm. Sajnani discourages her students from using AI to help brainstorm, but doesn’t mind when it writes for them. When asked if there’s a concern that all the essays will sound the same, she said her students are AI-native and have trained their AI chatbots to sound like them. And she said there’s been a spike in enrollment in her firm’s AI literacy program. “The reason we still have the admissions essay is to show a moment of growth. I think it’s less so about the writing and more so to show situations and how a student has grown from it,” Sajnani said. Some students aren’t totally sold on AI writing, but see its benefits for other parts of the admissions process. “I feel like when using AI, people want to think that you want to cheat the process,” Anisah Ali, a high school junior in Washington, told CNN. “I see it more as you want to open up ideas in your brain that you wouldn’t think about doing yourself.” Pallie does see a distant future where college essays don’t play as big a role. But, in a way, the replacement is even more person-facing than the essay. “In our ideal world, everyone would do an interview of some sort,” Pallie said. But the style of that interview? “Human.” But not all uses of AI in the college application process are as controversial. Leveling the playing field The college admissions process begins with deciding which schools are the best fit. In this case, AI can help students who are putting together applications on their own or whose families can’t afford to spend thousands on private college consultants. This year, ChatGPT launched a college planner for teens. OpenAI said the most popular prompts included “ask questions to develop my ideas,” “give feedback on my draft” and “help me check my evidence.” “For a lot of students, AI is the college counselor they can’t afford,” Michael Koppenheffer, chief innovation officer of enrollment solutions at EAB, told CNN. “They can get more information and they get more detailed guidance than they ever could before.” EAB found that AI plays the an outsized role in influencing what schools students applied to, compared to resources like college’s websites and search. Eighty-two percent of students surveyed in its AI report said they used ChatGPT when asked what AI tools they used in their college search. Christine Wilson, who already utilizes AI to help run her marketing agency in Virginia, at first hired a college counselor for her son, Ronan, who “built a list for him of initial schools that then we ended up kind of redoing ourselves using AI.” She used Claude to make a spreadsheet of the 22 universities Ronan applied to last year. The spreadsheet ran an analysis of the cost of attendance for each school, taking stats like income and potential aid into account. It saved Wilson “many, many hours of research,” she said. Wilson and her son ran a separate analysis for colleges that had football, Greek life and prestigious business schools. (Ronan ended up committing to The University of Florida.) Bunmi Emenanjo’s 17-year-old daughter has specific criteria for her future university: It has to be urban, offer merit aid and have a diverse student body. While she hired a college counselor for her older son, this year they are relying on Claude. “It’s just easier to use AI to search for that versus going through each school and digging up that information,” Emenanjo said. But for her family, the application itself will use more of the traditional methods – she said her daughter won’t be using AI for her essays.

articles.body: HoABL has repaid Rs 1,100 crore of the Rs 1,500-crore investment commitment made by HDFC Capital Advisors ahead of schedule, completing an early exit from five projects under their joint investment platform, following accelerated collections from project deliveries.The platform, established in 2023, covered 11 plotted development and low-rise projects across metros, Tier II cities and emerging markets. HDFC Capital committed around Rs 1,500 crore to the projects. Faster cash collections from completed developments, including Imperial Goa and Isle of Bliss, enabled the early repayment. HDFC Capital continues to have around Rs 400 crore deployed across the remaining six projects.The transaction marks the completion of an institutional investment cycle within six years of HoABL's establishment in 2020. Trustcap served as the sole financial advisor.The early repayment allows HoABL to retire institutional capital from five project entities, reducing its financing costs and giving it greater control over cash flows from the remaining inventory. In real estate private equity, early repayments are typically driven by project collections and contractual arrangements that prioritise the return of institutional capital.According to Vipul Roongta, CEO of HDFC Capital, the company was among HoABL's early investors and the returns reflect the partnerships it builds. "HDFC Capital has been an early investor in HoABL and the value creation on our investments reflects the strong partnerships that HDFC Capital builds," he said.HoABL chairman Abhinandan Lodha said the transaction reflected the company's approach to identifying real estate opportunities and managing investments through their lifecycle. He said the focus was on "actively working towards value creation throughout the investment lifecycle."The repayment also provides HoABL with a track record of returning institutional capital ahead of schedule, which could help it access funding from lenders and investors. Its direct-to-buyer model has sold more than 13 million sq ft to over 8,500 customers.However, the repayment also represents a cash outflow from project account.HoABL, which operates independently of the listed Lodha Group, has 25 million sq ft under development across five states.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Siege on Hebron’s Beit Ula industrial zone threatens Palestinian economy
articles.summary: Israel takes measures to crush Palestinian business in the occupied West Bank.
articles.body:
Beit Ula, occupied West Bank – Fayez al-Amleh, 63, scans his factory in an industrial complex in this town northwest of Hebron and reflects on the recent Israeli measures that could cost him his business.

The production lines at TB.LOC, which produce security and fire-resistant doors, still slowly whir away. But they very nearly came to a halt when Israeli forces sealed the entrances to the Beit Ula industrial zone with earthen berms and stone barriers on November 4.

The measures have isolated roughly 60 Palestinian businesses from their customers and suppliers, which threatens the livelihoods of 2,500 workers employed in the industrial zone.

“Today, raw materials cannot get in, and we cannot get our products out of the industrial zone,” al-Amleh told Al Jazeera.

Hebron and the surrounding areas were hit hard by Israeli military operations after two Israeli soldiers were killed by suspected Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city on October 23.

Thousands of Palestinians were forced out of their homes during the 10-day siege on Hebron and returned only when Israeli soldiers left the city on November 2 .

The siege on Hebron, an economic hub for the occupied West Bank, led to losses of more than 12 million shekels ($3.8m) a day, according to Hebron Mayor Yousef al-Jabari .

But just days after the siege on Hebron was lifted, the blockade on Beit Ula’s industrial zone began. This has significantly impacted the operations of al-Amleh’s factory and the lives of the 70 workers his business employs.

As a result, his employees have had their hours cut or moved to part-time work, reducing their take-home pay.

Since the closure, daily sales for al-Amleh’s business have dropped from 70,000 shekels ($21,988) to between 2,000 and 3,000 shekels ($628 to $942).

Beit Ula has facilities that shape metal and make doors, electrical cabinets, sponge, cardboard and construction materials. Their activities are connected to a wider network of commercial and service businesses that depend on the continued movement of supplies and goods.

Agricultural activities on the surrounding land have also been affected along with suppliers and traders whose daily business depends on the factories.

Israeli forces have carried out a series of measures around the town of Beit Ula, including the demolition of four industrial facilities and the establishment of a nearby settlement outpost.

These measures are viewed by Palestinians in the area as part of a broader Israeli effort to take control of land surrounding the industrial zone and threaten economic and agricultural activity in the area.

Al-Amleh said that if the siege on the industrial zone continues more factories could be forced to shut down. This would severely impact the economic viability of Beit Ula and nearby towns, which rely heavily on the industrial zone for employment and secondary businesses.

He rejected an allegation by Israel that Beit Ula is responsible for the movement of workers into Israel without work permits, the reason Israel has given for imposing restrictions on the industrial zone. Instead, he considers it to be a form of collective punishment against Palestinian businesses and workers based there.

Ayman al-Adam, who has worked at the industrial zone for about three years, said the Israeli blockade on Beit Ula threatens the incomes that he and hundreds of other employees rely on to support their families.

“This road closure is not just a closure. It is closing the doors of livelihood for all the workers,” he told Al Jazeera.

The Israeli military and settlers have embarked on a campaign of disruption and intimidation against Palestinian businesses across the West Bank in recent months.

Settler pogroms have seen West Bank olive farmers routinely attacked during this year’s harvest and Palestinian crops, olive trees and livestock stolen .

An expansion of Israeli checkpoints across the West Bank has also restricted the movement of goods and people, hitting Palestinian businesses hard .

Palestinian Minister of National Economy Mohammad al-Amour said the Israeli measures targeting economic facilities in the West Bank amount to a war on the Palestinian economy.

“About 60 economic facilities along with their workers and all aspects of their production have been completely isolated from the Palestinian economy,” al-Amour told Al Jazeera. “This situation has become a burden on the Palestinian economy instead of being a source of support and contributing to it.”

Mahmoud Allan, head of the North Hebron Chamber of Commerce and Industry, has appealed to authorities to halt the apparent Israeli campaign against Palestinian business.

“If this area is not reopened very quickly, some of the facilities that are major establishments in this licensed industrial zone in Beit Ula will be disrupted and forced to close,” he said.

“Factories can no longer operate normally. Workers have lost their income, and business owners are struggling to keep their businesses alive.”

articles.title: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia with a $132 billion stake — here's when he can sell and why investors may not know when he does: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Most of Huang's Nvidia shares are tied up with his wife, but the rules on who sees him sell are about to loosen.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang lost his job, but not his stock. Soon, investors may not be able to see him sell it.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board accepted Huang's resignation on Nov. 11. He walks away from about $108 million in unvested stock awards , pocket change next to the roughly 812 million shares he keeps, worth about $132 billion at Friday's close. That makes him Nvidia's largest individual owner.

When an insider sells, Wall Street sometimes reads it as a vote of no confidence in the company. When the founder of the world's most important AI chipmaker sells, the whole market can follow.

"This is no doubt an overhang on the trade for the foreseeable future," Liz Thomas, SoFi's chief market strategist, told Yahoo Finance on Thursday.

Investors are already voting. Nvidia stock closed Friday at its lowest level since July 2025, about 32% below its Oct. 6 record.

Legally, Huang can sell now. For three months after leaving, he still counts as a company insider, so any big sale needs a public notice filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission .

The legal cap on those sales won't slow him down. Based on trading before the scandal, it's about 600 million shares every three months, by Yahoo Finance calculations. That's more than eight times the shares he holds in his own name.

But only his own shares are easy to sell, and the insider-trading rules don't expire in February.

The concern with hidden sales is that a former CEO might know bad news before the public does. Trading on that is still illegal, notice or no notice, and brokers keep records of every trade, which regulators can check.

Most of the pile isn't his to move alone

About 70 million shares, worth about $11 billion, are in Huang's own name, according to his SEC filings . The other 740 million or so, worth about $121 billion, sit in family trusts, including one he runs with his wife, Lori. That setup makes a quick fire sale hard.

Even a full exit is smaller than it looks. His whole stake equals less than six days of typical Nvidia trading before the scandal, and Nvidia had $235 billion left on its buyback as of Sept. 28, enough to soak up every share he owns.

Why a 2-week window in February has come into focus

Nvidia typically reports fourth quarter results and files its annual report in late February. That leaves a gap of about two weeks after Huang's insider period ends, and that has drawn attention online.

Selling ahead of bad news he knew about would still be illegal.

Leaving doesn't erase his signature, either. Huang signed off on Nvidia's financial statements every quarter as CEO, and the quarter it reports Tuesday ended Oct. 25, on his watch.

articles.title: 'Massive shoes to fill': Wall Street sours on Nvidia stock after Jensen Huang's exit
articles.summary: As the market digested the unfolding drama at Nvidia, at least 10 analysts downgraded their Buy rating on the stock to Hold.
articles.body:
Wall Street analysts have had a change of heart on Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock following CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit on the heels of extramarital affairs , including one with a suspected spy and two employees.

As the market digested the unfolding drama, at least 10 analysts downgraded their Buy rating on the stock to Hold.

" The uncertainty proved too much for us; we moved to the sidelines on the stock," wrote Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon and his team on Thursday. "Nothing would give us more pleasure than being able to revisit the story at some point, but we are having a hard time advocating stepping in here."

The analyst, who slapped a Market Perform rating on the stock with a $200 price target, called into question the ability of any new CEO to truly fill Jensen's shoes "given how tightly he managed the direction of the business and its relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, and the broader industry ecosystem."

Until the board announced Huang's resignation, Wall Street had long grappled with Nvidia's one-man risk: a larger-than-life CEO whose role had come to seem irreplaceable to the company and the broader AI market.

"How can you have the world's most valuable company and no kind of succession plan, not even anyone being groomed with 60 people reporting to Jensen?" former Medtronic CEO Bill George told Yahoo Finance on Friday.

Downgrades on Wall Street cited uncertainty about the leadership change and its impact on the broader AI ecosystem.

"Huang's role as the 'face of AI' cannot be overstated," wrote Oppenheimer's Rich Schafer, downgrading the stock to a Hold as media reports of a second affair surfaced on Wednesday night. "We see massive shoes to fill and no obvious successor," he added.

Yorkville's Dan Ives, however, maintained an Outperform rating on the stock with a lowered price target of $225, writing that "we are not throwing in the white towel" on Nvidia.

Ives added that the "US tech industry is still way ahead of China in the AI Revolution, and this situation will sharpen the sword in the battle and arms race between the two countries."

Wall Street sees the Huang scandal raising the odds that Congress will push through new chip and chip-equipment export controls in December as Nvidia probes are in the works.

In the meantime, Nvidia will announce quarterly results on Tuesday, Nov. 17, with CFO Collette Kress serving as interim CEO until a permanent replacement is named. President Trump has called for former Apple ( AAPL ) CEO Tim Cook to step into the role.
